Arguments:

raw_counts: A matrix of raw gene expression counts (genes as rows,
          samples as columns). If ‘normalized = FALSE’, a matrix of
          TPM-normalized values instead (not log-transformed). Always
          required, also when ‘dt’, ‘tfs’ and ‘pathways’ are all
          supplied precomputed (its samples are checked against them).

  deconv: (Optional) A data frame with deconvolution features
          (cell-type proportions as columns x samples as rows). If
          ‘NULL’ (default), it is computed with
          ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’ using
          ‘deconv_methods’. Ignored if ‘dt’ is supplied.

      dt: (Optional) A precomputed cell-subgroup object, typically the
          output of ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’ (or
          the ‘Processed_deconvolution’ element returned by a previous
          ‘CellTFusion()’ run). If supplied, cell-type deconvolution
          and the deconvolution analysis step are both skipped and the
          pipeline proceeds straight to cell group construction using
          this object. It must have the same samples as ‘raw_counts’.

     tfs: (Optional) A precomputed TF activity matrix (samples as rows,
          TFs as columns), typically the ‘TFs_matrix’ element returned
          by a previous ‘CellTFusion()’ run or by
          ‘compute.TFs.activity()’. When ‘batch’ is given, a named list
          of such matrices (one per cohort). If supplied, TF activity
          inference is skipped.

pathways: (Optional) A precomputed pathway activity matrix, typically
          the ‘Pathways_scores’ element returned by a previous
          ‘CellTFusion()’ run or by ‘compute.pathway.activity()’. If
          supplied, pathway activity inference is skipped.

normalized: Logical; if TRUE (default), ‘raw_counts’ are raw counts and
          are normalized to log2(TPM + 1) for the TF activity and
          pathway activity steps (for deconvolution they are normalized
          to TPM only). If FALSE, ‘raw_counts’ must already be
          TPM-normalized and *not* log-transformed: the TPM values are
          used as they are for deconvolution and log2(TPM + 1) is
          computed internally for the other steps. Do not pass
          log-transformed values, as they would be log-transformed a
          second time (a warning is given when the values do not look
          like TPM, i.e. no value above 20 or negative values).

   batch: (Optional) A vector with the cohort of each sample (e.g.
          ‘coldata$Cohort’), in the same order as the columns of
          ‘raw_counts’; if it is named, it is matched to the samples by
          name instead. It is always treated as categorical. If given,
          the multi-cohort mode is run: TF and pathway activities are
          computed per cohort, TF modules are built from a consensus
          network across cohorts (see ‘consensus_quantile’), and the
          cohort is controlled for in the deconvolution analysis and
          cell group construction. Default is ‘NULL’ (single cohort); a
          vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.

deconv_methods: A character vector of deconvolution methods to apply.
          Default is ‘c("Quantiseq", "CBSX", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq",
          "DWLS")’. ‘"CBSX"’ (CIBERSORTx) is only run when ‘cbsx_mail’
          and ‘cbsx_token’ are given; otherwise it is skipped with a
          message.

cbsx_mail: (Optional) Email credential for CIBERSORTx. Needed to run
          "CBSX"; without it, CIBERSORTx is skipped.

cbsx_token: (Optional) Token credential for CIBERSORTx. Needed to run
          "CBSX"; without it, CIBERSORTx is skipped.

do_parallel: Logical; whether to run the deconvolution methods that
          support it (CIBERSORTx and DWLS) in parallel, one signature
          per worker (passed to ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’
          as ‘doParallel’). Default is FALSE.

 workers: (Optional) Number of parallel workers when ‘do_parallel =
          TRUE’. If ‘NULL’ (default), the number of available cores
          minus one is used.

file_name: (Optional) Name used in the output files saved in the
          "Results/" directory. If ‘NULL’ and ‘return = TRUE’,
          ‘"CellTFusion"’ is used.

TF.collection: Character. The source of the TF-target network. Options
          are ‘"CollecTRI"’ (default), ‘"Dorothea"’, or ‘"ARACNE"’.

            • ‘"CollecTRI"’ uses the prebuilt collection from OmnipathR
              and ‘"Dorothea"’ the one from the ‘dorothea’ package.

            • ‘"ARACNE"’ reads a network file (tab-separated with
              ‘Regulator’ and ‘Target’ columns, and a ‘mor’ column with
              the sign of each interaction; see
              ‘compute.TFs.activity()’) from
              ‘input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt’.

  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the TFs
          and the PROGENy pathways: ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model,
          default), ‘"mlm"’ (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’
          (weighted sum) or ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three).
          Passed to ‘compute.TFs.activity()’ and
          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’.

min_targets_size: Integer. Minimum number of target genes per regulon,
          passed to ‘compute.TFs.activity()’. Default is 5.

universe: Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target
          interactions (columns ‘source’, ‘target’ and ‘mor’, the mode
          of regulation: 1 activation, -1 repression). If not provided,
          the function will fetch the relevant network based on the
          ‘TF.collection’ argument.

   paths: Optional. A user-specified data frame of pathways gene sets.
          If not provided, the function will fetch the relevant
          pathways based on ‘PROGENy’.

gene_sets: Optional. A named list of custom gene sets (character
          vectors of gene symbols) passed to
          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’'s ‘gene_sets’ argument for
          GSVA-based scoring. If ‘NULL’, only PROGENy is used.

min_module_size: Integer; minimum module size for WGCNA module
          detection. Default is 5.

corr_mod: Numeric; correlation threshold for merging TF modules.
          Default is 0.9.

soft_power: (Optional) Soft-thresholding power used to build the TF
          network, passed to ‘compute.WTCNA()’: one value, or one value
          per cohort (in the order the cohorts first appear in ‘batch’)
          in multi-cohort mode. If ‘NULL’ (default), it is chosen
          automatically.

consensus_quantile: Numeric between 0 and 1, used in multi-cohort mode
          only: quantile of the topological overlaps of each pair of
          TFs across cohorts used as their consensus (0, the default,
          is the minimum: two TFs are close only if they are close in
          every cohort; higher values are less strict). Passed to
          ‘compute.WTCNA()’.

clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clusterings
          (‘stats::hclust()’): of the TFs, to build the TF modules
          (‘compute.WTCNA()’), and of the deconvolution features of
          each TF module, to build the cell groups
          (‘construct_cell_groups()’). Default is ‘"ward.D2"’.

    corr: Numeric; correlation threshold used in the deconvolution
          analysis. Default is 0.7.

corr_type: Correlation type used in every step that computes
          correlations: ‘"spearman"’ (default) or ‘"pearson"’. Passed
          to ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’
          (deconvolution subgroups), ‘compute.WTCNA()’ (TF network and
          module merging) and ‘construct_cell_groups()’ (correlation
          between TF modules and deconvolution features).

cells_extra: (Optional) A character vector with the cell names to
          consider that are not included in the nomenclature of
          multideconv (see R package). This includes the group names
          created with ‘multideconv::aggregate_cell_groups()’ on
          ‘deconv’ (e.g. ‘"Lymphocytes"’): if they are not listed here
          they are discarded.

    pval: Numeric; p-value threshold used when building cell groups
          (selection of the deconvolution features significantly
          correlated with each TF module). Default is 0.05.

    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values used when building cell groups
          are corrected for multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg,
          across the deconvolution features for each TF module) and
          compared with ‘pval’. Passed to ‘construct_cell_groups()’.
          Default is FALSE.

min_cluster_size: Integer; minimum number of features of a cell group
          (minimum cluster size of the dynamic tree cut), passed to
          ‘construct_cell_groups()’. Default is 3.

compute_factors: Logical. If TRUE (default), the NMF latent factors
          (‘compute.latent_factors()’) and the cell niches
          (‘compute_cells_niches()’) are computed from the cell group
          scores. If FALSE, they are skipped (‘Latent_spaces’ and
          ‘Cells_niches’ are ‘NULL’), e.g. in the cross-validation
          folds of ‘prepare_celltfusion_folds()’, where only the cell
          group scores are used.

   top_n: Integer. Number of top-contributing cell groups per NMF
          factor in the cell niches (see ‘compute_cells_niches()’).
          Default is 5.

cancer_type: Character. Cancer type abbreviation (e.g. ‘"skcm"’), only
          used when ‘TF.collection = "ARACNE"’, to locate the ARACNe
          network at ‘input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt’.
          If ‘NULL’, the network is auto-detected when only one exists
          under ‘input/ARACNE/’.

  return: Logical; if TRUE, intermediate matrices and plots are written
          to the "Results/" folder. Default is TRUE.

 verbose: Logical; whether to print the progress and the console output
          and messages of every step (warnings are always shown).
          Default is TRUE.

    seed: Integer. Random seed of the pipeline (deconvolution methods
          with random steps and NMF), so that results are reproducible.
          Default is 123.

Details:

     The pipeline runs with a fixed random seed (‘seed’) so results are
     reproducible; the caller's random number generator state is
     restored when the function returns. With ‘normalized = TRUE’,
     sample names are converted with ‘make.names()’ (e.g.
     ‘"TCGA-XX-1234"’ becomes ‘"TCGA.XX.1234"’), as
     ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’ also does; ‘deconv’ rows
     are matched to the samples in either form.

Value:

     A list containing:

     Deconvolution A matrix with cell-type proportions (samples as
          rows, cell types as columns); ‘NULL’ if ‘dt’ was supplied
          without ‘deconv’.

     TFs_matrix A matrix with TF activity scores (samples as rows, TFs
          as columns), or a list of matrices (one per cohort) when
          ‘batch’ is given. Single cohort: raw scores (not scaled),
          which do not depend on the other samples (e.g. for machine
          learning features, to be scaled with the training samples).
          With ‘batch’: scores z-scored within each cohort (correction
          of cohort shifts).

     TF_network The TF module network returned by ‘compute.WTCNA()’.
          Its module matrix is always in the sample order of
          ‘raw_counts’ (also in multi-cohort mode).

     Pathways_scores Pathway activity scores returned by
          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’: raw in single-cohort mode,
          z-scored within each cohort with ‘batch’ (as ‘TFs_matrix’).

     Processed_deconvolution The processed deconvolution subgroups
          (output of ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’).

     Cell_groups Output of ‘construct_cell_groups()’: cell group
          scores, compositions and projection weights.

     Latent_spaces NMF latent factors returned by
          ‘compute.latent_factors()’ (‘NULL’ with ‘compute_factors =
          FALSE’).

     Cells_niches Top cell groups of each latent factor, with their
          deconvolution features and CCA coefficients (see
          ‘compute_cells_niches()’; ‘NULL’ with ‘compute_factors =
          FALSE’).

Examples:

     ## Not run:
     
     data("raw.counts.tuto")
     
     res <- CellTFusion(
       raw_counts = raw.counts.tuto,
       normalized = TRUE,
       deconv_methods = c("Quantiseq", "DeconRNASeq"),
       file_name = "TestRun",
       min_targets_size = 15,
       min_module_size = 20,
       corr_mod = 0.25,
       corr = 0.7,
       pval = 0.05
     )
     
     # Re-run with previously computed features, skipping straight to cell group construction
     res2 <- CellTFusion(
       raw_counts = raw.counts.tuto,
       dt = res$Processed_deconvolution,
       tfs = res$TFs_matrix,
       pathways = res$Pathways_scores,
       normalized = TRUE,
       file_name = "TestRun_rerun",
       min_module_size = 20,
       corr_mod = 0.25,
       pval = 0.05
     )
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.TFs.activity
Compute Transcription Factor (TF) activity

Description:

     Infers transcription factor (TF) activity from a gene expression
     matrix with ‘decoupleR::decouple()’ (Badia-i-Mompel et al., 2022).
     By default the univariate linear model (‘"ulm"’) is used. The
     TF-target network can be provided by the user, obtained from
     prebuilt collections (CollecTRI from OmnipathR or Dorothea from
     the ‘dorothea’ package), or read from an ARACNe-inferred network.

Usage:

     compute.TFs.activity(
       counts_norm,
       TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
       min_targets_size = 5,
       universe = NULL,
       cancer_type = NULL,
       method = "ulm",
       scale = TRUE,
       return = TRUE,
       file_name = NULL
     )
     
Arguments:

counts_norm: A gene expression matrix with genes (symbols) as rows and
          samples as columns, with unique sample names. The matrix
          should be log-normalized (e.g., log2(TPM + 1), log2CPM,
          etc.). A warning is given if it has values above 20, which
          log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.

TF.collection: Character. The source of the TF-target network. Options
          are ‘"CollecTRI"’ (default), ‘"Dorothea"’, or ‘"ARACNE"’.

            • ‘"CollecTRI"’ uses the prebuilt collection from OmnipathR
              and ‘"Dorothea"’ (confidence A and B) the one from the
              ‘dorothea’ package. Each collection is cached in its own
              file, Results/TF_target_collection_<TF.collection>.csv,
              and reused on later calls: a message gives the number of
              TFs and interactions of the cached file and the date it
              was saved. A cached file that is empty or lacks the
              columns ‘source’, ‘target’ and ‘mor’ is not used (the
              collection is obtained again, with a warning). Delete the
              file to obtain the collection again.

            • ‘"ARACNE"’ reads a tab-separated network file with
              ‘Regulator’ and ‘Target’ columns from
              input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt (relative
              to the working directory). The mode of regulation of each
              edge is read from a ‘mor’ column of the file (1
              activation, -1 repression), which should be the sign of
              the Spearman correlation between TF and target computed
              on the cohort used to build the network. If the file has
              no ‘mor’ column, a warning is given and the signs are
              computed as the sign of the Spearman correlation between
              TF and target in the samples of ‘counts_norm’; they then
              depend on the samples given (e.g. they can differ between
              cohorts, or between a training and a test set).

min_targets_size: Integer. Minimum number of target genes per regulon
          (passed to ‘decoupleR::decouple()’ as ‘minsize’). Default is
          5.

universe: Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target
          interactions (columns ‘source’, ‘target’, ‘mor’). The three
          columns are required: ‘mor’ is the mode of regulation (1
          activation, -1 repression; use 1 for every edge if the
          network has no sign). If not provided, the network is fetched
          based on ‘TF.collection’. Ignored when ‘TF.collection =
          "ARACNE"’.

cancer_type: Optional character. TCGA cancer type abbreviation used to
          locate the ARACNe network (only used when ‘TF.collection =
          "ARACNE"’). If ‘NULL’, the network is auto-detected when only
          one ‘network.txt’ exists under ‘input/ARACNE/’.

  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the TFs:
          ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model, default), ‘"mlm"’
          (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’ (weighted sum) or
          ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three).

   scale: Logical. If TRUE (default), z-score scales the TF activity
          matrix across samples. The scaled scores of a sample then
          depend on the other samples given in the same call; use
          ‘scale = FALSE’ to get scores that can be compared between
          separate calls (e.g. a training and a test set). With fewer
          than three samples the scores are not scaled (a message is
          given).

  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves matrix in Results/ folder. Default is
          TRUE.

file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing the TF activity
          matrix to disk (‘Results/TF_matrix_<file_name>.csv’; without
          it, ‘Results/TF_matrix.csv’).

Value:

     A data frame of inferred (and, if ‘scale = TRUE’, scaled) TF
     activity scores, with samples as rows and TFs as columns. Column
     names are made syntactically valid with ‘make.names()’ (e.g.
     ‘NKX2.1’), in the returned table and in the saved file.

References:

     Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of
     computational methods to infer biological activities from omics
     data. _Bioinformatics Advances_, 2(1), vbac016.
     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

     Tuerei, D., Korcsmaros, T., & Saez-Rodriguez, J. (2016). OmniPath:
     guidelines and gateway for literature-curated signaling pathway
     resources. _Nature Methods_, 13(12), 966-967.
     https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4077

     Garcia-Alonso, L. et al. (2019). Benchmark and integration of
     resources for the estimation of human transcription factor
     activities. _Genome Research_.
     https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.240663.118

     Lachmann, A. et al. (2016). ARACNe-AP: gene network reverse
     engineering through adaptive partitioning inference of mutual
     information. _Bioinformatics_, 32(14), 2233-2235.
     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw216

     Margolin, A.A. et al. (2006). ARACNE: an algorithm for the
     reconstruction of gene regulatory networks in a mammalian cellular
     context. _BMC Bioinformatics_, 7(Suppl 1), S7.
     https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-7-S1-S7

Examples:

     ## Not run:
     
     # Downloads the CollecTRI network from OmniPath
     data("counts.norm.tuto")
     tfs_activity <- compute.TFs.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.pathway.activity
Compute pathway activity scores

Description:

     This function computes pathway activity scores from log-normalized
     gene expression data with ‘decoupleR’ (Badia-i-Mompel et al.,
     2022), based on the PROGENy resource (Schubert et al., 2018). By
     default the univariate linear model (‘"ulm"’) is used. Optionally,
     it also performs Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) using hallmark
     signatures or any user-provided gene sets.

Usage:

     compute.pathway.activity(
       counts_norm,
       gene_sets = NULL,
       paths = NULL,
       method = "ulm",
       scale = TRUE,
       batch = NULL,
       return = TRUE,
       file_name = NULL
     )
     
Arguments:

counts_norm: A numeric matrix of log-normalized gene expression values
          (e.g. log2(TPM + 1)) with genes (symbols) as rows and samples
          as columns. A warning is given if it has values above 20,
          which log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.

gene_sets: A named list of gene sets (character vectors of gene
          symbols; e.g., hallmark signatures or user-defined sets). If
          provided, GSVA scores will be computed for these sets.
          Default is ‘NULL’.

   paths: A data frame describing the pathway-gene interactions
          (columns ‘source’, ‘target’, ‘weight’) for use with PROGENy.
          If ‘NULL’, the human PROGENy resource (top 500 genes) is used
          and cached in ‘Results/Pathways_collection_PROGENy.csv’ (also
          when ‘return = FALSE’, so that it is downloaded only once). A
          message gives the number of pathways and interactions of the
          cached file and the date it was saved; a cached file that is
          empty or lacks the needed columns is not used (the collection
          is downloaded again, with a warning). Delete the file to
          download the collection again.

  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the
          PROGENy pathways: ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model, default),
          ‘"mlm"’ (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’ (weighted sum)
          or ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three). The gene sets of
          ‘gene_sets’ are always scored with GSVA.

   scale: Logical. If TRUE (default), each pathway is z-scored across
          the samples. The scaled scores of a sample then depend on the
          other samples given in the same call; use ‘scale = FALSE’ to
          get scores that can be compared between separate calls (e.g.
          a training and a test set). With fewer than three samples the
          scores are not scaled (a message is given).

   batch: Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the column
          order of ‘counts_norm’ (if it is named, it is matched to the
          samples by name instead). It is always treated as
          categorical. If given, the samples are split by cohort, the
          pathway activities (PROGENy and, if requested, GSVA) are
          computed and scaled (see ‘scale’) separately in each cohort,
          and the results are joined in the sample order of
          ‘counts_norm’; the output has the same form as without
          ‘batch’. Pathways or gene sets that cannot be scored in every
          cohort are left out (with a message). Default is ‘NULL’
          (single cohort); a vector with only one cohort is treated the
          same way.

  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves the score matrices in Results/
          folder. Default is TRUE.

file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing output CSV files
          (‘Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy_<file_name>.csv’ and
          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA_<file_name>.csv’; without it,
          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy.csv’ and
          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA.csv’).

Value:

     If ‘gene_sets’ is ‘NULL’, a data frame of PROGENy pathway activity
     scores (samples as rows, pathways as columns), scaled if ‘scale =
     TRUE’. If ‘gene_sets’ is provided, a list with two elements:

        • ‘PROGENy’: A data frame of PROGENy pathway activity scores.

        • ‘GSVA’: A data frame of GSVA scores based on the provided
          gene sets.

     Column names are made syntactically valid with ‘make.names()’
     (e.g. ‘JAK.STAT’), in the returned tables and in the saved files.
     Pathways with fewer than 5 of their genes in the data, and gene
     sets that GSVA cannot score, are left out with a message.

References:

     Schubert M, Klinger B, Kluenemann M, Sieber A, Uhlitz F, Sauer S,
     Garnett MJ, Bluethgen N, Saez-Rodriguez J. Perturbation-response
     genes reveal signaling footprints in cancer gene expression.
     Nature Communications. 2018. doi:10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
     <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6>

     Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of
     computational methods to infer biological activities from omics
     data. _Bioinformatics Advances_, 2(1), vbac016.
     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

Examples:

     ## Not run:
     
     # Compute only PROGENy activities (downloads the PROGENy model from OmniPath)
     data("counts.norm.tuto")
     pathways <- compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.WTCNA

Description:

     Construct a weighted signed or unsigned network using TF activity
     to cluster protein regulators into modules that share similar
     activity patterns. Each TF module will have a sample-level score

       network_type = "signed",
       clustering_method = "ward.D2",

       file_name = NULL,
       soft_power = NULL,
       consensus_quantile = 0,
       return = TRUE
     )

          are standardized (within each cohort with ‘batch’) to compute
          the module eigengenes, and the other steps use correlations,
          which do not depend on the scaling. With ‘batch’, the TF
          activities of all the cohorts, each computed within its
          cohort (as ‘CellTFusion()’ does).

   batch: (Optional) A vector with the cohort of each sample, in the
          row order of ‘tfs’; if it is named, it is matched to the
          samples by name instead. It is always treated as categorical.
          If given, consensus TF modules are built across the cohorts
          (see Details) and module eigengenes are computed and scaled
          within each cohort. Default is ‘NULL’ (single cohort); a
          vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.

network_type: Network type: "signed" (default) or "unsigned".

clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering of the

166	          vectors of gene symbols) passed to
167	          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’'s ‘gene_sets’ argument for
168	          GSVA-based scoring. If ‘NULL’, only PROGENy is used.
169	
170	min_module_size: Integer; minimum module size for WGCNA module
171	          detection. Default is 5.
172	
173	corr_mod: Numeric; correlation threshold for merging TF modules.
174	          Default is 0.9.
175	
176	soft_power: (Optional) Soft-thresholding power used to build the TF
177	          network, passed to ‘compute.WTCNA()’: one value, or one value
178	          per cohort (in the order the cohorts first appear in ‘batch’)
179	          in multi-cohort mode. If ‘NULL’ (default), it is chosen
180	          automatically.
181	
182	consensus_quantile: Numeric between 0 and 1, used in multi-cohort mode
183	          only: quantile of the topological overlaps of each pair of
184	          TFs across cohorts used as their consensus (0, the default,
185	          is the minimum: two TFs are close only if they are close in
186	          every cohort; higher values are less strict). Passed to
187	          ‘compute.WTCNA()’.
188	
189	clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clusterings
190	          (‘stats::hclust()’): of the TFs, to build the TF modules
191	          (‘compute.WTCNA()’), and of the deconvolution features of
192	          each TF module, to build the cell groups
193	          (‘construct_cell_groups()’). Default is ‘"ward.D2"’.
194	
195	    corr: Numeric; correlation threshold used in the deconvolution
196	          analysis. Default is 0.7.
197	
198	corr_type: Correlation type used in every step that computes
199	          correlations: ‘"spearman"’ (default) or ‘"pearson"’. Passed
200	          to ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’
201	          (deconvolution subgroups), ‘compute.WTCNA()’ (TF network and
202	          module merging) and ‘construct_cell_groups()’ (correlation
203	          between TF modules and deconvolution features).
204	
205	cells_extra: (Optional) A character vector with the cell names to
206	          consider that are not included in the nomenclature of
207	          multideconv (see R package). This includes the group names
208	          created with ‘multideconv::aggregate_cell_groups()’ on
209	          ‘deconv’ (e.g. ‘"Lymphocytes"’): if they are not listed here
210	          they are discarded.
211	
212	    pval: Numeric; p-value threshold used when building cell groups
213	          (selection of the deconvolution features significantly
214	          correlated with each TF module). Default is 0.05.
215	
216	    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values used when building cell groups
217	          are corrected for multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg,
218	          across the deconvolution features for each TF module) and
219	          compared with ‘pval’. Passed to ‘construct_cell_groups()’.
220	          Default is FALSE.
221	
222	min_cluster_size: Integer; minimum number of features of a cell group
223	          (minimum cluster size of the dynamic tree cut), passed to
224	          ‘construct_cell_groups()’. Default is 3.
225	
226	compute_factors: Logical. If TRUE (default), the NMF latent factors
227	          (‘compute.latent_factors()’) and the cell niches
228	          (‘compute_cells_niches()’) are computed from the cell group
229	          scores. If FALSE, they are skipped (‘Latent_spaces’ and
230	          ‘Cells_niches’ are ‘NULL’), e.g. in the cross-validation
231	          folds of ‘prepare_celltfusion_folds()’, where only the cell
232	          group scores are used.
233	
234	   top_n: Integer. Number of top-contributing cell groups per NMF
235	          factor in the cell niches (see ‘compute_cells_niches()’).
236	          Default is 5.
237	
238	cancer_type: Character. Cancer type abbreviation (e.g. ‘"skcm"’), only
239	          used when ‘TF.collection = "ARACNE"’, to locate the ARACNe
240	          network at ‘input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt’.
241	          If ‘NULL’, the network is auto-detected when only one exists
242	          under ‘input/ARACNE/’.
243	
244	  return: Logical; if TRUE, intermediate matrices and plots are written
245	          to the "Results/" folder. Default is TRUE.
246	
247	 verbose: Logical; whether to print the progress and the console output
248	          and messages of every step (warnings are always shown).
249	          Default is TRUE.
250	
251	    seed: Integer. Random seed of the pipeline (deconvolution methods
252	          with random steps and NMF), so that results are reproducible.
253	          Default is 123.
254	
255	Details:
256	
257	     The pipeline runs with a fixed random seed (‘seed’) so results are
258	     reproducible; the caller's random number generator state is
259	     restored when the function returns. With ‘normalized = TRUE’,
260	     sample names are converted with ‘make.names()’ (e.g.
261	     ‘"TCGA-XX-1234"’ becomes ‘"TCGA.XX.1234"’), as
262	     ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’ also does; ‘deconv’ rows
263	     are matched to the samples in either form.
264	
265	Value:
266	
267	     A list containing:
268	
269	     Deconvolution A matrix with cell-type proportions (samples as
270	          rows, cell types as columns); ‘NULL’ if ‘dt’ was supplied
271	          without ‘deconv’.
272	
273	     TFs_matrix A matrix with TF activity scores (samples as rows, TFs
274	          as columns), or a list of matrices (one per cohort) when
275	          ‘batch’ is given. Single cohort: raw scores (not scaled),
276	          which do not depend on the other samples (e.g. for machine
277	          learning features, to be scaled with the training samples).
278	          With ‘batch’: scores z-scored within each cohort (correction
279	          of cohort shifts).
280	
281	     TF_network The TF module network returned by ‘compute.WTCNA()’.
282	          Its module matrix is always in the sample order of
283	          ‘raw_counts’ (also in multi-cohort mode).
284	
285	     Pathways_scores Pathway activity scores returned by
286	          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’: raw in single-cohort mode,
287	          z-scored within each cohort with ‘batch’ (as ‘TFs_matrix’).
288	
289	     Processed_deconvolution The processed deconvolution subgroups
290	          (output of ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’).
291	
292	     Cell_groups Output of ‘construct_cell_groups()’: cell group
293	          scores, compositions and projection weights.
294	
295	     Latent_spaces NMF latent factors returned by
296	          ‘compute.latent_factors()’ (‘NULL’ with ‘compute_factors =
297	          FALSE’).
298	
299	     Cells_niches Top cell groups of each latent factor, with their
300	          deconvolution features and CCA coefficients (see
301	          ‘compute_cells_niches()’; ‘NULL’ with ‘compute_factors =
302	          FALSE’).
303	
304	Examples:
305	
306	     ## Not run:
307	     
308	     data("raw.counts.tuto")
309	     
310	     res <- CellTFusion(
311	       raw_counts = raw.counts.tuto,
312	       normalized = TRUE,
313	       deconv_methods = c("Quantiseq", "DeconRNASeq"),
314	       file_name = "TestRun",
315	       min_targets_size = 15,
316	       min_module_size = 20,
317	       corr_mod = 0.25,
318	       corr = 0.7,
319	       pval = 0.05
320	     )
321	     
322	     # Re-run with previously computed features, skipping straight to cell group construction
323	     res2 <- CellTFusion(
324	       raw_counts = raw.counts.tuto,
325	       dt = res$Processed_deconvolution,
326	       tfs = res$TFs_matrix,
327	       pathways = res$Pathways_scores,
328	       normalized = TRUE,
329	       file_name = "TestRun_rerun",
330	       min_module_size = 20,
331	       corr_mod = 0.25,
332	       pval = 0.05
333	     )
334	     ## End(Not run)

336	=========== compute.TFs.activity
337	Compute Transcription Factor (TF) activity
338	
339	Description:
340	
341	     Infers transcription factor (TF) activity from a gene expression
342	     matrix with ‘decoupleR::decouple()’ (Badia-i-Mompel et al., 2022).
343	     By default the univariate linear model (‘"ulm"’) is used. The
344	     TF-target network can be provided by the user, obtained from
345	     prebuilt collections (CollecTRI from OmnipathR or Dorothea from
346	     the ‘dorothea’ package), or read from an ARACNe-inferred network.
347	
348	Usage:
349	
350	     compute.TFs.activity(
351	       counts_norm,
352	       TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
353	       min_targets_size = 5,
354	       universe = NULL,
355	       cancer_type = NULL,
356	       method = "ulm",
357	       scale = TRUE,
358	       return = TRUE,
359	       file_name = NULL
360	     )
361	     
362	Arguments:
363	
364	counts_norm: A gene expression matrix with genes (symbols) as rows and
365	          samples as columns, with unique sample names. The matrix
366	          should be log-normalized (e.g., log2(TPM + 1), log2CPM,
367	          etc.). A warning is given if it has values above 20, which
368	          log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.
369	
370	TF.collection: Character. The source of the TF-target network. Options
371	          are ‘"CollecTRI"’ (default), ‘"Dorothea"’, or ‘"ARACNE"’.
372	
373	            • ‘"CollecTRI"’ uses the prebuilt collection from OmnipathR
374	              and ‘"Dorothea"’ (confidence A and B) the one from the
375	              ‘dorothea’ package. Each collection is cached in its own
376	              file, Results/TF_target_collection_<TF.collection>.csv,
377	              and reused on later calls: a message gives the number of
378	              TFs and interactions of the cached file and the date it
379	              was saved. A cached file that is empty or lacks the
380	              columns ‘source’, ‘target’ and ‘mor’ is not used (the
381	              collection is obtained again, with a warning). Delete the
382	              file to obtain the collection again.
383	
384	            • ‘"ARACNE"’ reads a tab-separated network file with
385	              ‘Regulator’ and ‘Target’ columns from
386	              input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt (relative
387	              to the working directory). The mode of regulation of each
388	              edge is read from a ‘mor’ column of the file (1
389	              activation, -1 repression), which should be the sign of
390	              the Spearman correlation between TF and target computed
391	              on the cohort used to build the network. If the file has
392	              no ‘mor’ column, a warning is given and the signs are
393	              computed as the sign of the Spearman correlation between
394	              TF and target in the samples of ‘counts_norm’; they then
395	              depend on the samples given (e.g. they can differ between
396	              cohorts, or between a training and a test set).
397	
398	min_targets_size: Integer. Minimum number of target genes per regulon
399	          (passed to ‘decoupleR::decouple()’ as ‘minsize’). Default is
400	          5.
401	
402	universe: Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target
403	          interactions (columns ‘source’, ‘target’, ‘mor’). The three
404	          columns are required: ‘mor’ is the mode of regulation (1
405	          activation, -1 repression; use 1 for every edge if the
406	          network has no sign). If not provided, the network is fetched
407	          based on ‘TF.collection’. Ignored when ‘TF.collection =
408	          "ARACNE"’.
409	
410	cancer_type: Optional character. TCGA cancer type abbreviation used to
411	          locate the ARACNe network (only used when ‘TF.collection =
412	          "ARACNE"’). If ‘NULL’, the network is auto-detected when only
413	          one ‘network.txt’ exists under ‘input/ARACNE/’.
414	
415	  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the TFs:
416	          ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model, default), ‘"mlm"’
417	          (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’ (weighted sum) or
418	          ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three).
419	
420	   scale: Logical. If TRUE (default), z-score scales the TF activity
421	          matrix across samples. The scaled scores of a sample then
422	          depend on the other samples given in the same call; use
423	          ‘scale = FALSE’ to get scores that can be compared between
424	          separate calls (e.g. a training and a test set). With fewer
425	          than three samples the scores are not scaled (a message is
426	          given).
427	
428	  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves matrix in Results/ folder. Default is
429	          TRUE.
430	
431	file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing the TF activity
432	          matrix to disk (‘Results/TF_matrix_<file_name>.csv’; without
433	          it, ‘Results/TF_matrix.csv’).
434	
435	Value:
436	
437	     A data frame of inferred (and, if ‘scale = TRUE’, scaled) TF
438	     activity scores, with samples as rows and TFs as columns. Column
439	     names are made syntactically valid with ‘make.names()’ (e.g.
440	     ‘NKX2.1’), in the returned table and in the saved file.
441	
442	References:
443	
444	     Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of
445	     computational methods to infer biological activities from omics
446	     data. _Bioinformatics Advances_, 2(1), vbac016.
447	     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
448	
449	     Tuerei, D., Korcsmaros, T., & Saez-Rodriguez, J. (2016). OmniPath:
450	     guidelines and gateway for literature-curated signaling pathway
451	     resources. _Nature Methods_, 13(12), 966-967.
452	     https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4077
453	
454	     Garcia-Alonso, L. et al. (2019). Benchmark and integration of
455	     resources for the estimation of human transcription factor
456	     activities. _Genome Research_.
457	     https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.240663.118
458	
459	     Lachmann, A. et al. (2016). ARACNe-AP: gene network reverse
460	     engineering through adaptive partitioning inference of mutual
461	     information. _Bioinformatics_, 32(14), 2233-2235.
462	     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw216
463	
464	     Margolin, A.A. et al. (2006). ARACNE: an algorithm for the
465	     reconstruction of gene regulatory networks in a mammalian cellular
466	     context. _BMC Bioinformatics_, 7(Suppl 1), S7.
467	     https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-7-S1-S7
468	
469	Examples:
470	
471	     ## Not run:
472	     
473	     # Downloads the CollecTRI network from OmniPath
474	     data("counts.norm.tuto")
475	     tfs_activity <- compute.TFs.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
476	     ## End(Not run)

478	=========== compute.pathway.activity
479	Compute pathway activity scores
480	
481	Description:
482	
483	     This function computes pathway activity scores from log-normalized
484	     gene expression data with ‘decoupleR’ (Badia-i-Mompel et al.,
485	     2022), based on the PROGENy resource (Schubert et al., 2018). By
486	     default the univariate linear model (‘"ulm"’) is used. Optionally,
487	     it also performs Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) using hallmark
488	     signatures or any user-provided gene sets.
489	
490	Usage:
491	
492	     compute.pathway.activity(
493	       counts_norm,
494	       gene_sets = NULL,
495	       paths = NULL,
496	       method = "ulm",
497	       scale = TRUE,
498	       batch = NULL,
499	       return = TRUE,
500	       file_name = NULL
501	     )
502	     
503	Arguments:
504	
505	counts_norm: A numeric matrix of log-normalized gene expression values
506	          (e.g. log2(TPM + 1)) with genes (symbols) as rows and samples
507	          as columns. A warning is given if it has values above 20,
508	          which log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.
509	
510	gene_sets: A named list of gene sets (character vectors of gene
511	          symbols; e.g., hallmark signatures or user-defined sets). If
512	          provided, GSVA scores will be computed for these sets.
513	          Default is ‘NULL’.
514	
515	   paths: A data frame describing the pathway-gene interactions
516	          (columns ‘source’, ‘target’, ‘weight’) for use with PROGENy.
517	          If ‘NULL’, the human PROGENy resource (top 500 genes) is used
518	          and cached in ‘Results/Pathways_collection_PROGENy.csv’ (also
519	          when ‘return = FALSE’, so that it is downloaded only once). A
520	          message gives the number of pathways and interactions of the
521	          cached file and the date it was saved; a cached file that is
522	          empty or lacks the needed columns is not used (the collection
523	          is downloaded again, with a warning). Delete the file to
524	          download the collection again.
525	
526	  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the
527	          PROGENy pathways: ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model, default),
528	          ‘"mlm"’ (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’ (weighted sum)
529	          or ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three). The gene sets of
530	          ‘gene_sets’ are always scored with GSVA.
531	
532	   scale: Logical. If TRUE (default), each pathway is z-scored across
533	          the samples. The scaled scores of a sample then depend on the
534	          other samples given in the same call; use ‘scale = FALSE’ to
535	          get scores that can be compared between separate calls (e.g.
536	          a training and a test set). With fewer than three samples the
537	          scores are not scaled (a message is given).
538	
539	   batch: Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the column
540	          order of ‘counts_norm’ (if it is named, it is matched to the
541	          samples by name instead). It is always treated as
542	          categorical. If given, the samples are split by cohort, the
543	          pathway activities (PROGENy and, if requested, GSVA) are
544	          computed and scaled (see ‘scale’) separately in each cohort,
545	          and the results are joined in the sample order of
546	          ‘counts_norm’; the output has the same form as without
547	          ‘batch’. Pathways or gene sets that cannot be scored in every
548	          cohort are left out (with a message). Default is ‘NULL’
549	          (single cohort); a vector with only one cohort is treated the
550	          same way.
551	
552	  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves the score matrices in Results/
553	          folder. Default is TRUE.
554	
555	file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing output CSV files
556	          (‘Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy_<file_name>.csv’ and
557	          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA_<file_name>.csv’; without it,
558	          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy.csv’ and
559	          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA.csv’).
560	
561	Value:
562	
563	     If ‘gene_sets’ is ‘NULL’, a data frame of PROGENy pathway activity
564	     scores (samples as rows, pathways as columns), scaled if ‘scale =
565	     TRUE’. If ‘gene_sets’ is provided, a list with two elements:
566	
567	        • ‘PROGENy’: A data frame of PROGENy pathway activity scores.
568	
569	        • ‘GSVA’: A data frame of GSVA scores based on the provided
570	          gene sets.
571	
572	     Column names are made syntactically valid with ‘make.names()’
573	     (e.g. ‘JAK.STAT’), in the returned tables and in the saved files.
574	     Pathways with fewer than 5 of their genes in the data, and gene
575	     sets that GSVA cannot score, are left out with a message.
576	
577	References:
578	
579	     Schubert M, Klinger B, Kluenemann M, Sieber A, Uhlitz F, Sauer S,
580	     Garnett MJ, Bluethgen N, Saez-Rodriguez J. Perturbation-response
581	     genes reveal signaling footprints in cancer gene expression.
582	     Nature Communications. 2018. doi:10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
583	     <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6>
584	
585	     Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of
586	     computational methods to infer biological activities from omics
587	     data. _Bioinformatics Advances_, 2(1), vbac016.
588	     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
589	
590	Examples:
591	
592	     ## Not run:
593	     
594	     # Compute only PROGENy activities (downloads the PROGENy model from OmniPath)
595	     data("counts.norm.tuto")
596	     pathways <- compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
597	     ## End(Not run)

599	=========== compute.WTCNA
600	Compute Weighted TF-coactivity Network Analysis (WTCNA)
601	
602	Description:
603	
604	     Construct a weighted signed or unsigned network using TF activity
605	     to cluster protein regulators into modules that share similar
606	     activity patterns. Each TF module will have a sample-level score
607	     represented by the eigengene of the module.
608	
609	Usage:
610	
611	     compute.WTCNA(
612	       tfs,
613	       batch = NULL,
614	       network_type = "signed",
615	       clustering_method = "ward.D2",
616	       min_module_size = 5,
617	       corr_mod = 0.9,
618	       corr_type = "spearman",
619	       verbose = TRUE,
620	       file_name = NULL,
621	       soft_power = NULL,
622	       consensus_quantile = 0,
623	       return = TRUE
624	     )
625	     
626	Arguments:
627	
628	     tfs: Matrix of TF activity (samples x TFs), scaled or not: the TFs
629	          are standardized (within each cohort with ‘batch’) to compute
630	          the module eigengenes, and the other steps use correlations,
631	          which do not depend on the scaling. With ‘batch’, the TF
632	          activities of all the cohorts, each computed within its
633	          cohort (as ‘CellTFusion()’ does).
634	
635	   batch: (Optional) A vector with the cohort of each sample, in the
636	          row order of ‘tfs’; if it is named, it is matched to the
637	          samples by name instead. It is always treated as categorical.
638	          If given, consensus TF modules are built across the cohorts
639	          (see Details) and module eigengenes are computed and scaled
640	          within each cohort. Default is ‘NULL’ (single cohort); a
641	          vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.
642	
643	network_type: Network type: "signed" (default) or "unsigned".
644	
645	clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering of the
646	          TFs (‘stats::hclust()’), applied to the TOM dissimilarity (1
647	          - topological overlap) between TFs, or to the consensus TOM
648	          dissimilarity in batch mode. Default is "ward.D2" (WGCNA's
649	          own default is "average": two groups of TFs are joined
650	          according to the average dissimilarity between their TFs).
651	
652	min_module_size: Minimum number of TFs per module. Default is 5.
653	
654	corr_mod: Correlation threshold (0-1): modules whose eigengenes have a
655	          correlation (of type ‘corr_type’) above it are merged. In
656	          batch mode, the correlation is computed on the eigengenes of
657	          all the samples, scaled within each cohort. Default is 0.9.
658	
659	corr_type: Correlation used to pick the soft-threshold power, build the
660	          adjacency matrix, merge modules and compute the proportion of
661	          variance explained: "spearman" (default) or "pearson", in
662	          single-cohort and batch mode. The module eigengene is always
663	          the first principal component of the module's TF activities.
664	
665	 verbose: Logical; whether to print the function messages. Default is
666	          TRUE.
667	
668	file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing WTCNA outputs
669	          (CSV files and, in single-cohort mode, the diagnostic plots
670	          ‘Soft_Threshold_<file_name>.pdf’,
671	          ‘Gene_dendrogram_and_module_colors_<file_name>.pdf’ and
672	          ‘Gene_dendrogram_and_module_colors_after_merging_<file_name>.pdf’).
673	
674	soft_power: Optional numeric value specifying the soft-thresholding
675	          power used to build the adjacency matrix (one value per
676	          cohort, in the order the cohorts first appear in ‘batch’, in
677	          batch mode). If ‘NULL’, the lowest power whose scale-free fit
678	          R^2 reaches 0.9 is chosen automatically (the power with the
679	          best fit if none reaches 0.9, with a message).
680	
681	consensus_quantile: Numeric between 0 and 1 (batch mode only). For each
682	          pair of TFs, the consensus topological overlap is this
683	          quantile of its (calibrated) topological overlaps across the
684	          cohorts. With 0 (default), the minimum: two TFs are close
685	          only if they are close in every cohort, the strictest choice,
686	          which removes more TF relationships as more cohorts are
687	          added. Higher values are less strict: with ‘K’ cohorts,
688	          ‘consensus_quantile = k / (K - 1)’ takes the ‘(k + 1)’-th
689	          lowest value, so two TFs are close if they are close in all
690	          cohorts but ‘k’ (e.g. 0.25 with 5 cohorts: in at least 4 of
691	          them); 0.5 is the median.
692	
693	  return: Logical, whether to save output plots, the module list
694	          (‘Results/TFs_modules_<file_name>.csv’) and the module matrix
695	          (‘Results/TF_module_matrix_<file_name>.csv’, with the sample
696	          names as row names) to "Results/" (without ‘file_name’,
697	          ‘TFs_modules.csv’ and ‘TF_module_matrix.csv’). Default is
698	          TRUE.
699	
700	Details:
701	
702	     TFs that WGCNA does not assign to any module (color ‘"grey"’) are
703	     not a module: they are left out of the module matrix and of ‘TFs
704	     per module’, with a message.
705	
706	     In batch mode, the modules are built with the same steps as in
707	     single-cohort mode, on a consensus network:
708	
709	       1. the samples are split by cohort, and a soft-thresholding
710	          power is chosen for each cohort;
711	
712	       2. the adjacency and the topological overlap matrix (TOM) are
713	          computed in each cohort, with its own power;
714	
715	       3. the TOMs are calibrated to a common scale as in
716	          ‘WGCNA::blockwiseConsensusModules()’: each TOM is raised to
717	          the power that makes its 0.95 quantile equal to that of the
718	          first cohort;
719	
720	       4. the consensus TOM is, for each pair of TFs, the
721	          ‘consensus_quantile’ quantile of its calibrated TOMs across
722	          cohorts;
723	
724	       5. the TFs are clustered on 1 - consensus TOM with
725	          ‘clustering_method’ and the tree is cut with the same dynamic
726	          tree cut as in single-cohort mode;
727	
728	       6. the module eigengenes are computed and scaled within each
729	          cohort, and the modules are merged as in single-cohort mode
730	          (see ‘corr_mod’); merged scores are scaled within each cohort
731	          again.
732	
733	     Unlike ‘WGCNA::blockwiseConsensusModules()’, the TFs of each
734	     module are not filtered or reassigned afterwards by their module
735	     membership (as in single-cohort mode). The diagnostic plots are
736	     only saved in single-cohort mode.
737	
738	Value:
739	
740	     A named list with:
741	
742	        • ‘TFs module matrix’: Scaled module eigengenes (samples x
743	          modules), in the row order of ‘tfs’.
744	
745	        • ‘TFs colors’: Vector of module colors assigned to each TF
746	          (‘"grey"’ for TFs not assigned to any module).
747	
748	        • ‘TFs per module’: List of TF names in each module.
749	
750	        • ‘Proportion of variance’: Variance explained per module
751	          (single-cohort mode only).
752	
753	        • ‘TFs_matrix’: The TF activity matrix used (a list of
754	          per-cohort matrices in batch mode, in the order the cohorts
755	          first appear in ‘batch’).
756	
757	        • ‘Network parameters’: A list with the soft-thresholding
758	          power(s) used (‘soft_power’, one per cohort in batch mode),
759	          ‘network_type’ and ‘corr_type’, used by ‘identify_hub_TFs()’,
760	          and in batch mode ‘consensus_quantile’.
761	
762	References:
763	
764	     Langfelder, P., & Horvath, S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for
765	     weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559.
766	     https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-9-559
767	
768	Examples:
769	
770	     data("tfs.tuto")
771	     network <- compute.WTCNA(tfs.tuto, corr_mod = 0.9, return = FALSE)
772	     
773	=========== identify.cell.groups
774	Identify cell groups
775	
776	Description:
777	
778	     Builds, for each TF module, a dendrogram of the deconvolution
779	     features significantly correlated with it. The features are
780	     clustered on the value of that correlation: the distance between
781	     two features is the absolute difference between their correlations
782	     with the module (e.g. 0.62 and 0.58 are at distance 0.04). Two
783	     features are therefore similar when they are related to the module
784	     to the same degree (similar biological activity), not when they
785	     vary together across samples. The dendrograms are cut into cell
786	     groups by ‘cell.groups.computation()’.
787	
788	Usage:
789	
790	     ## S3 method for class 'cell.groups'
791	     identify(
792	       relationship,
793	       clustering_method = "ward.D2",
794	       file_name = NULL,
795	       return = TRUE
796	     )
797	     
798	Arguments:
799	
800	relationship: The list returned by ‘compute.modules.relationship()’.
801	          Its first two elements are used (accessed by position):
802	
803	            • ‘[[1]]’ (‘correlation’): A matrix of correlations between
804	              TF modules (rows, named) and deconvolution features
805	              (columns).
806	
807	            • ‘[[2]]’ (‘significant’): A list, named by TF module, of
808	              the features significantly correlated with each module
809	              (p-value, or adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’, <= the
810	              ‘pval’ given to ‘compute.modules.relationship()’).
811	
812	          The correlations of each module are taken from the row with
813	          its name.
814	
815	clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering
816	          (‘stats::hclust()’) of the features on the distance described
817	          above. Default: "ward.D2".
818	
819	file_name: Optional character suffix for the names of the saved plots.
820	
821	  return: Logical; whether to save one dendrogram plot per module to
822	          ‘Results/Dendrogram_cell_types_<module>_<file_name>.pdf’
823	          (‘Results/Dendrogram_cell_types_<module>.pdf’ without
824	          ‘file_name’). Each plot shows the correlation of every
825	          feature with the module next to its name, and its size
826	          follows the number of features. Default: TRUE.
827	
828	Value:
829	
830	     A named list of dendrograms (‘hclust’ objects, labelled with the
831	     feature names), one per TF module. Each one also stores the
832	     correlation of its features with the module (element
833	     ‘correlation’, used by ‘calculate_dendrogram_cuts()’). Modules
834	     with fewer than two significant features are discarded; ‘NULL’ is
835	     returned if no module remains.
836	
837	Examples:
838	
839	     data("network.tuto")
840	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
841	     rel <- compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]], deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]], return = FALSE)
842	     dendrograms <- identify.cell.groups(rel, return = FALSE)
843	     names(dendrograms)
844	     
845	=========== compute.modules.relationship
846	Compute modules relationship
847	
848	Description:
849	
850	     Correlates every column of one matrix with every column of another
851	     (e.g., TF modules and external features such as deconvolution
852	     estimates or pathway activities) across the same set of samples,
853	     and visualizes the significant associations. It is meant for
854	     continuous variables only: all the columns of both matrices must
855	     be numeric. For categorical variables (e.g. clinical groups), use
856	     ‘compute.metadata.association()’.
857	
858	Usage:
859	
860	     compute.modules.relationship(
861	       matA,
862	       matB,
863	       file_name = NULL,
864	       batch = NULL,
865	       pval = 0.05,
866	       padj = FALSE,
867	       corr_type = "spearman",
868	       vertical = FALSE,
869	       return = TRUE,
870	       plot_grid = FALSE,
871	       ncol_grid = NULL
872	     )
873	     
874	Arguments:
875	
876	    matA: A numeric matrix or data frame of continuous features
877	          (samples x features), e.g. TF module scores.
878	
879	    matB: A numeric matrix or data frame of continuous features to
880	          correlate with (samples x features).
881	
882	file_name: A string indicating the base name (without extension) of the
883	          figures to be saved in the "Results/" folder. If ‘NULL’
884	          (default), no figure is saved.
885	
886	   batch: Optional vector indicating batch assignment for samples (no
887	          missing values). If it has two or more levels, partial
888	          correlations (‘ppcor::pcor.test()’, Pearson or Spearman
889	          according to ‘corr_type’) are computed controlling for batch.
890	          Batch is treated as categorical (one dummy variable per level
891	          beyond the first).
892	
893	    pval: A numeric threshold for the p-value to define significance
894	          (p-value, or adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’, <= ‘pval’).
895	          Default is 0.05.
896	
897	    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple
898	          testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, across the
899	          columns of ‘matB’ for each column of ‘matA’, and the adjusted
900	          p-values are used to define significance (in ‘significant’
901	          and in the figures). Default is FALSE.
902	
903	corr_type: Type of correlation to compute: "spearman" (default) or
904	          "pearson". It also sets the type of the partial correlations
905	          computed with ‘batch’.
906	
907	vertical: Logical; if TRUE, modules are on the x-axis and the ‘matB’
908	          features on the y-axis. Otherwise (default), the ‘matB’
909	          features are on the x-axis and modules on the y-axis.
910	
911	  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves the heatmap plot as a PDF
912	          (‘file_name’ is needed). Default is TRUE.
913	
914	plot_grid: Logical; if TRUE, generates per-pair scatter grid plots for
915	          significant associations, saved to
916	          "Results/<file_name>_scatter_grid.svg" (the 100 strongest
917	          pairs at most). With Spearman, the ranks of the values are
918	          shown, as the correlation is computed on them. With ‘batch’,
919	          the values shown are corrected for batch, as the correlations
920	          are. Default is FALSE.
921	
922	ncol_grid: Integer number of columns used in scatter grid layout. If
923	          NULL (default), it is set to the ceiling of the square root
924	          of the number of panels.
925	
926	Details:
927	
928	     ‘matA’ and ‘matB’ must have the same samples in the same order
929	     (same rownames); names are compared after ‘make.names()’, so e.g.
930	     "TCGA-XX" and "TCGA.XX" match. Correlations and p-values use, for
931	     each pair of columns, the samples with a value in both (missing
932	     values are allowed); a pair with fewer than three such samples, or
933	     without variation among them, gets ‘NA’. Columns without variation
934	     are skipped with a message. Column names must be unique within
935	     each matrix.
936	
937	Value:
938	
939	     Invisibly, a list with:
940	
941	        • ‘correlation’: the correlation matrix (columns of ‘matA’ as
942	          rows, columns of ‘matB’ as columns).
943	
944	        • ‘significant’: a named list with, for each column of ‘matA’,
945	          the columns of ‘matB’ significantly correlated with it
946	          (p-value, or adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’, <= ‘pval’).
947	
948	        • ‘p_value’: the matrix of p-values.
949	
950	        • ‘p_adjusted’: the matrix of Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted
951	          p-values (equal to ‘p_value’ with ‘padj = FALSE’).
952	
953	     If ‘return = TRUE’ and ‘file_name’ is given, a heatmap of the
954	     correlations is saved to "Results/<file_name>.pdf" (the ".pdf"
955	     extension is added if missing). Its size is computed from the
956	     number of features. With up to 40 features per axis, the
957	     significant cells show the correlation and its significance (* <
958	     0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001, **** < 0.0001); with more, they are
959	     marked with an asterisk.
960	
961	Examples:
962	
963	     data("network.tuto")
964	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
965	     corr = compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]],
966	                                         deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]],
967	                                         return = FALSE,
968	                                         pval = 0.01)
969	     corr$correlation[1:3, 1:3]
970	     corr$significant[[1]]
971	     
972	     ## Not run:
973	     
974	     # TF modules vs PROGENy pathways (downloads the PROGENy model from OmniPath)
975	     data("counts.norm.tuto")
976	     pathways <- compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
977	     compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]],
978	                                  pathways,
979	                                  "Pathways_Progeny-TFs_Modules")
980	     ## End(Not run)
981	     
982	=========== compute.metadata.association
983	Compute associations between TF module scores and clinical metadata
984	
985	Description:
986	
987	     This function tests for associations between transcription factor
988	     (TF) module scores and available clinical traits. Numeric traits
989	     are correlated with each module (Pearson or Spearman) and shown as
990	     a heatmap. If ‘plot_grid = TRUE’, categorical traits (text, factor
991	     and TRUE/FALSE columns) are additionally tested with one-way ANOVA
992	     (Tukey HSD post-hoc) and shown as boxplot grids. All plots are
993	     saved in the Results/ directory, and the tables with the results
994	     are returned.
995	
996	Usage:
997	
998	     compute.metadata.association(
999	       scores,
1000	       coldata,
1001	       pval = 0.05,
1002	       corr_type = "spearman",
1003	       file_name = NULL,
1004	       ncol_grid = NULL,
1005	       plot_grid = FALSE,
1006	       padj = FALSE
1007	     )
1008	     
1009	Arguments:
1010	
1011	  scores: A numeric matrix or data frame of TF module scores across
1012	          samples. Typically the first element (TFs module matrix) of
1013	          the output from ‘compute.WTCNA()’. Rows represent samples,
1014	          columns represent TF modules.
1015	
1016	 coldata: A data frame containing clinical traits (both categorical and
1017	          numerical) for the same samples. Rows must be the same
1018	          samples, in the same order, as the rows of ‘scores’ (checked
1019	          by name; an error is raised otherwise). Numeric columns are
1020	          treated as continuous: convert number-coded categories (e.g.
1021	          a stage coded 1 to 4) to factor to test them as groups.
1022	
1023	    pval: A numeric threshold (default = 0.05) to determine statistical
1024	          significance (p-value, or adjusted p-value, ‘<= pval’). Only
1025	          associations with (adjusted) p-values below this threshold
1026	          are annotated in the heatmap or drawn as boxplots.
1027	
1028	corr_type: Correlation used for the numeric traits: ‘"spearman"’
1029	          (default) or ‘"pearson"’.
1030	
1031	file_name: Optional character suffix of the names of the saved plots
1032	          (‘NULL’ by default: no suffix).
1033	
1034	ncol_grid: Integer. Number of columns in the grid of association
1035	          boxplots. If ‘NULL’ (default), it is set to the ceiling of
1036	          the square root of the number of panels.
1037	
1038	plot_grid: Logical; if TRUE, tests categorical traits with ANOVA and
1039	          saves boxplot grids. Default is FALSE.
1040	
1041	    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple
1042	          testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, across the
1043	          modules for each trait, and the adjusted p-values are
1044	          compared with ‘pval’. Default is FALSE.
1045	
1046	Details:
1047	
1048	     Traits that cannot be tested are skipped with a message: numeric
1049	     traits without variation, and categorical traits with a single
1050	     level or with as many levels as samples (e.g. a sample
1051	     identifier). Categorical traits are only analysed when ‘plot_grid
1052	     = TRUE’; a message lists them otherwise.
1053	
1054	     The size of the figures is computed from their content (number of
1055	     modules and traits for the heatmap, number of panels for the
1056	     boxplot grids), and the y-axis of each boxplot panel from its
1057	     data.
1058	
1059	Value:
1060	
1061	     Invisibly, a list with the results:
1062	
1063	        • ‘correlation’: matrix of module-trait correlations for the
1064	          numeric traits (modules x traits).
1065	
1066	        • ‘p_value’: matrix of their p-values.
1067	
1068	        • ‘p_adjusted’: matrix of their Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted
1069	          p-values (equal to ‘p_value’ with ‘padj = FALSE’).
1070	
1071	        • ‘anova’: data frame with the ANOVA of every module for every
1072	          categorical trait (‘trait’, ‘module’, ‘F’, ‘p’,
1073	          ‘p_adjusted’); ‘NULL’ if ‘plot_grid = FALSE’.
1074	
1075	     The elements are ‘NULL’ when there is no trait of that type. The
1076	     following files are saved to the Results/ directory:
1077	
1078	        • ‘TF.modules_metadata_<file_name>.pdf’: a heatmap of
1079	          module-trait correlations for numeric traits (only
1080	          associations with p-value <= ‘pval’ are annotated, with the
1081	          correlation and its significance: * < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** <
1082	          0.001, **** < 0.0001).
1083	
1084	        • ‘ANOVA_boxplot_summary_<file_name>_<trait>.svg’ (if
1085	          ‘plot_grid = TRUE’): one boxplot grid per categorical trait
1086	          with the significant modules.
1087	
1088	Examples:
1089	
1090	     data("network.tuto")
1091	     data("traitdata.tuto")
1092	     
1093	     # Categorical traits (response, Enrollment.IC) are tested with plot_grid = TRUE; os and censOS are numeric
1094	     res <- compute.metadata.association(
1095	       scores = network.tuto[[1]],
1096	       coldata = traitdata.tuto,
1097	       pval = 0.05,
1098	       file_name = 'Tutorial',
1099	       plot_grid = TRUE
1100	     )
1101	     head(res$anova)
1102	     
1103
