=========== CellTFusion
Compute one-step CellTFusion

Description:

     Runs the full CellTFusion pipeline in a single call: cell-type
     deconvolution, TF activity inference, TF module construction,
     pathway activity, cell group construction, NMF latent factors and
     cell niches.

Usage:

     CellTFusion(
       raw_counts,
       deconv = NULL,
       dt = NULL,
       tfs = NULL,
       pathways = NULL,
       normalized = TRUE,
       batch = NULL,
       deconv_methods = c("Quantiseq", "CBSX", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
       cbsx_mail = NULL,
       cbsx_token = NULL,
       do_parallel = FALSE,
       workers = NULL,
       file_name = NULL,
       TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
       method = "ulm",
       min_targets_size = 5,
       universe = NULL,
       paths = NULL,
       gene_sets = NULL,
       min_module_size = 5,
       corr_mod = 0.9,
       soft_power = NULL,
       consensus_quantile = 0,
       clustering_method = "ward.D2",
       corr = 0.7,
       corr_type = "spearman",
       cells_extra = NULL,
       pval = 0.05,
       padj = FALSE,
       min_cluster_size = 3,
       compute_factors = TRUE,
       top_n = 5,
       cancer_type = NULL,
       return = TRUE,
       verbose = TRUE,
       seed = 123
     )
     
Arguments:

raw_counts: A matrix of raw gene expression counts (genes as rows,
          samples as columns). If ‘normalized = FALSE’, a matrix of
          TPM-normalized values instead (not log-transformed). Always
          required, also when ‘dt’, ‘tfs’ and ‘pathways’ are all
          supplied precomputed (its samples are checked against them).

  deconv: (Optional) A data frame with deconvolution features
          (cell-type proportions as columns x samples as rows). If
          ‘NULL’ (default), it is computed with
          ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’ using
          ‘deconv_methods’. Ignored if ‘dt’ is supplied.

      dt: (Optional) A precomputed cell-subgroup object, typically the
          output of ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’ (or
          the ‘Processed_deconvolution’ element returned by a previous
          ‘CellTFusion()’ run). If supplied, cell-type deconvolution
          and the deconvolution analysis step are both skipped and the
          pipeline proceeds straight to cell group construction using
          this object. It must have the same samples as ‘raw_counts’.

     tfs: (Optional) A precomputed TF activity matrix (samples as rows,
          TFs as columns), typically the ‘TFs_matrix’ element returned
          by a previous ‘CellTFusion()’ run or by
          ‘compute.TFs.activity()’. When ‘batch’ is given, a named list
          of such matrices (one per cohort). If supplied, TF activity
          inference is skipped.

pathways: (Optional) A precomputed pathway activity matrix, typically
          the ‘Pathways_scores’ element returned by a previous
          ‘CellTFusion()’ run or by ‘compute.pathway.activity()’. If
          supplied, pathway activity inference is skipped.

normalized: Logical; if TRUE (default), ‘raw_counts’ are raw counts and
          are normalized to log2(TPM + 1) for the TF activity and
          pathway activity steps (for deconvolution they are normalized
          to TPM only). If FALSE, ‘raw_counts’ must already be
          TPM-normalized and *not* log-transformed: the TPM values are
          used as they are for deconvolution and log2(TPM + 1) is
          computed internally for the other steps. Do not pass
          log-transformed values, as they would be log-transformed a
          second time (a warning is given when the values do not look
          like TPM, i.e. no value above 20 or negative values).

   batch: (Optional) A vector with the cohort of each sample (e.g.
          ‘coldata$Cohort’), in the same order as the columns of
          ‘raw_counts’; if it is named, it is matched to the samples by
          name instead. It is always treated as categorical. If given,
          the multi-cohort mode is run: TF and pathway activities are
          computed per cohort, TF modules are built from a consensus
          network across cohorts (see ‘consensus_quantile’), and the
          cohort is controlled for in the deconvolution analysis and
          cell group construction. Default is ‘NULL’ (single cohort); a
          vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.

deconv_methods: A character vector of deconvolution methods to apply.
          Default is ‘c("Quantiseq", "CBSX", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq",
          "DWLS")’. ‘"CBSX"’ (CIBERSORTx) is only run when ‘cbsx_mail’
          and ‘cbsx_token’ are given; otherwise it is skipped with a
          message.

cbsx_mail: (Optional) Email credential for CIBERSORTx. Needed to run
          "CBSX"; without it, CIBERSORTx is skipped.

cbsx_token: (Optional) Token credential for CIBERSORTx. Needed to run
          "CBSX"; without it, CIBERSORTx is skipped.

do_parallel: Logical; whether to run the deconvolution methods that
          support it (CIBERSORTx and DWLS) in parallel, one signature
          per worker (passed to ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’
          as ‘doParallel’). Default is FALSE.

 workers: (Optional) Number of parallel workers when ‘do_parallel =
          TRUE’. If ‘NULL’ (default), the number of available cores
          minus one is used.

file_name: (Optional) Name used in the output files saved in the
          "Results/" directory. If ‘NULL’ and ‘return = TRUE’,
          ‘"CellTFusion"’ is used.

TF.collection: Character. The source of the TF-target network. Options
          are ‘"CollecTRI"’ (default), ‘"Dorothea"’, or ‘"ARACNE"’.

            • ‘"CollecTRI"’ uses the prebuilt collection from OmnipathR
              and ‘"Dorothea"’ the one from the ‘dorothea’ package.

            • ‘"ARACNE"’ reads a network file (tab-separated with
              ‘Regulator’ and ‘Target’ columns, and a ‘mor’ column with
              the sign of each interaction; see
              ‘compute.TFs.activity()’) from
              ‘input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt’.

  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the TFs
          and the PROGENy pathways: ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model,
          default), ‘"mlm"’ (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’
          (weighted sum) or ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three).
          Passed to ‘compute.TFs.activity()’ and
          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’.

min_targets_size: Integer. Minimum number of target genes per regulon,
          passed to ‘compute.TFs.activity()’. Default is 5.

universe: Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target
          interactions (columns ‘source’, ‘target’ and ‘mor’, the mode
          of regulation: 1 activation, -1 repression). If not provided,
          the function will fetch the relevant network based on the
          ‘TF.collection’ argument.

   paths: Optional. A user-specified data frame of pathways gene sets.
          If not provided, the function will fetch the relevant
          pathways based on ‘PROGENy’.

gene_sets: Optional. A named list of custom gene sets (character
          vectors of gene symbols) passed to
          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’'s ‘gene_sets’ argument for
          GSVA-based scoring. If ‘NULL’, only PROGENy is used.

min_module_size: Integer; minimum module size for WGCNA module
          detection. Default is 5.

corr_mod: Numeric; correlation threshold for merging TF modules.
          Default is 0.9.

soft_power: (Optional) Soft-thresholding power used to build the TF
          network, passed to ‘compute.WTCNA()’: one value, or one value
          per cohort (in the order the cohorts first appear in ‘batch’)
          in multi-cohort mode. If ‘NULL’ (default), it is chosen
          automatically.

consensus_quantile: Numeric between 0 and 1, used in multi-cohort mode
          only: quantile of the topological overlaps of each pair of
          TFs across cohorts used as their consensus (0, the default,
          is the minimum: two TFs are close only if they are close in
          every cohort; higher values are less strict). Passed to
          ‘compute.WTCNA()’.

clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clusterings
          (‘stats::hclust()’): of the TFs, to build the TF modules
          (‘compute.WTCNA()’), and of the deconvolution features of
          each TF module, to build the cell groups
          (‘construct_cell_groups()’). Default is ‘"ward.D2"’.

    corr: Numeric; correlation threshold used in the deconvolution
          analysis. Default is 0.7.

corr_type: Correlation type used in every step that computes
          correlations: ‘"spearman"’ (default) or ‘"pearson"’. Passed
          to ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’
          (deconvolution subgroups), ‘compute.WTCNA()’ (TF network and
          module merging) and ‘construct_cell_groups()’ (correlation
          between TF modules and deconvolution features).

cells_extra: (Optional) A character vector with the cell names to
          consider that are not included in the nomenclature of
          multideconv (see R package). This includes the group names
          created with ‘multideconv::aggregate_cell_groups()’ on
          ‘deconv’ (e.g. ‘"Lymphocytes"’): if they are not listed here
          they are discarded.

    pval: Numeric; p-value threshold used when building cell groups
          (selection of the deconvolution features significantly
          correlated with each TF module). Default is 0.05.

    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values used when building cell groups
          are corrected for multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg,
          across the deconvolution features for each TF module) and
          compared with ‘pval’. Passed to ‘construct_cell_groups()’.
          Default is FALSE.

min_cluster_size: Integer; minimum number of features of a cell group
          (minimum cluster size of the dynamic tree cut), passed to
          ‘construct_cell_groups()’. Default is 3.

compute_factors: Logical. If TRUE (default), the NMF latent factors
          (‘compute.latent_factors()’) and the cell niches
          (‘compute_cells_niches()’) are computed from the cell group
          scores. If FALSE, they are skipped (‘Latent_spaces’ and
          ‘Cells_niches’ are ‘NULL’), e.g. in the cross-validation
          folds of ‘prepare_celltfusion_folds()’, where only the cell
          group scores are used.

   top_n: Integer. Number of top-contributing cell groups per NMF
          factor in the cell niches (see ‘compute_cells_niches()’).
          Default is 5.

cancer_type: Character. Cancer type abbreviation (e.g. ‘"skcm"’), only
          used when ‘TF.collection = "ARACNE"’, to locate the ARACNe
          network at ‘input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt’.
          If ‘NULL’, the network is auto-detected when only one exists
          under ‘input/ARACNE/’.

  return: Logical; if TRUE, intermediate matrices and plots are written
          to the "Results/" folder. Default is TRUE.

 verbose: Logical; whether to print the progress and the console output
          and messages of every step (warnings are always shown).
          Default is TRUE.

    seed: Integer. Random seed of the pipeline (deconvolution methods
          with random steps and NMF), so that results are reproducible.
          Default is 123.

Details:

     The pipeline runs with a fixed random seed (‘seed’) so results are
     reproducible; the caller's random number generator state is
     restored when the function returns. With ‘normalized = TRUE’,
     sample names are converted with ‘make.names()’ (e.g.
     ‘"TCGA-XX-1234"’ becomes ‘"TCGA.XX.1234"’), as
     ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution()’ also does; ‘deconv’ rows
     are matched to the samples in either form.

Value:

     A list containing:

     Deconvolution A matrix with cell-type proportions (samples as
          rows, cell types as columns); ‘NULL’ if ‘dt’ was supplied
          without ‘deconv’.

     TFs_matrix A matrix with TF activity scores (samples as rows, TFs
          as columns), or a list of matrices (one per cohort) when
          ‘batch’ is given. Single cohort: raw scores (not scaled),
          which do not depend on the other samples (e.g. for machine
          learning features, to be scaled with the training samples).
          With ‘batch’: scores z-scored within each cohort (correction
          of cohort shifts).

     TF_network The TF module network returned by ‘compute.WTCNA()’.
          Its module matrix is always in the sample order of
          ‘raw_counts’ (also in multi-cohort mode).

     Pathways_scores Pathway activity scores returned by
          ‘compute.pathway.activity()’: raw in single-cohort mode,
          z-scored within each cohort with ‘batch’ (as ‘TFs_matrix’).

     Processed_deconvolution The processed deconvolution subgroups
          (output of ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’).

     Cell_groups Output of ‘construct_cell_groups()’: cell group
          scores, compositions and projection weights.

     Latent_spaces NMF latent factors returned by
          ‘compute.latent_factors()’ (‘NULL’ with ‘compute_factors =
          FALSE’).

     Cells_niches Top cell groups of each latent factor, with their
          deconvolution features and CCA coefficients (see
          ‘compute_cells_niches()’; ‘NULL’ with ‘compute_factors =
          FALSE’).

Examples:

     ## Not run:
     
     data("raw.counts.tuto")
     
     res <- CellTFusion(
       raw_counts = raw.counts.tuto,
       normalized = TRUE,
       deconv_methods = c("Quantiseq", "DeconRNASeq"),
       file_name = "TestRun",
       min_targets_size = 15,
       min_module_size = 20,
       corr_mod = 0.25,
       corr = 0.7,
       pval = 0.05
     )
     
     # Re-run with previously computed features, skipping straight to cell group construction
     res2 <- CellTFusion(
       raw_counts = raw.counts.tuto,
       dt = res$Processed_deconvolution,
       tfs = res$TFs_matrix,
       pathways = res$Pathways_scores,
       normalized = TRUE,
       file_name = "TestRun_rerun",
       min_module_size = 20,
       corr_mod = 0.25,
       pval = 0.05
     )
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.TFs.activity
Compute Transcription Factor (TF) activity

Description:

     Infers transcription factor (TF) activity from a gene expression
     matrix with ‘decoupleR::decouple()’ (Badia-i-Mompel et al., 2022).
     By default the univariate linear model (‘"ulm"’) is used. The
     TF-target network can be provided by the user, obtained from
     prebuilt collections (CollecTRI from OmnipathR or Dorothea from
     the ‘dorothea’ package), or read from an ARACNe-inferred network.

Usage:

     compute.TFs.activity(
       counts_norm,
       TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
       min_targets_size = 5,
       universe = NULL,
       cancer_type = NULL,
       method = "ulm",
       scale = TRUE,
       return = TRUE,
       file_name = NULL
     )
     
Arguments:

counts_norm: A gene expression matrix with genes (symbols) as rows and
          samples as columns, with unique sample names. The matrix
          should be log-normalized (e.g., log2(TPM + 1), log2CPM,
          etc.). A warning is given if it has values above 20, which
          log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.

TF.collection: Character. The source of the TF-target network. Options
          are ‘"CollecTRI"’ (default), ‘"Dorothea"’, or ‘"ARACNE"’.

            • ‘"CollecTRI"’ uses the prebuilt collection from OmnipathR
              and ‘"Dorothea"’ (confidence A and B) the one from the
              ‘dorothea’ package. Each collection is cached in its own
              file, Results/TF_target_collection_<TF.collection>.csv,
              and reused on later calls: a message gives the number of
              TFs and interactions of the cached file and the date it
              was saved. A cached file that is empty or lacks the
              columns ‘source’, ‘target’ and ‘mor’ is not used (the
              collection is obtained again, with a warning). Delete the
              file to obtain the collection again.

            • ‘"ARACNE"’ reads a tab-separated network file with
              ‘Regulator’ and ‘Target’ columns from
              input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt (relative
              to the working directory). The mode of regulation of each
              edge is read from a ‘mor’ column of the file (1
              activation, -1 repression), which should be the sign of
              the Spearman correlation between TF and target computed
              on the cohort used to build the network. If the file has
              no ‘mor’ column, a warning is given and the signs are
              computed as the sign of the Spearman correlation between
              TF and target in the samples of ‘counts_norm’; they then
              depend on the samples given (e.g. they can differ between
              cohorts, or between a training and a test set).

min_targets_size: Integer. Minimum number of target genes per regulon
          (passed to ‘decoupleR::decouple()’ as ‘minsize’). Default is
          5.

universe: Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target
          interactions (columns ‘source’, ‘target’, ‘mor’). The three
          columns are required: ‘mor’ is the mode of regulation (1
          activation, -1 repression; use 1 for every edge if the
          network has no sign). If not provided, the network is fetched
          based on ‘TF.collection’. Ignored when ‘TF.collection =
          "ARACNE"’.

cancer_type: Optional character. TCGA cancer type abbreviation used to
          locate the ARACNe network (only used when ‘TF.collection =
          "ARACNE"’). If ‘NULL’, the network is auto-detected when only
          one ‘network.txt’ exists under ‘input/ARACNE/’.

  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the TFs:
          ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model, default), ‘"mlm"’
          (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’ (weighted sum) or
          ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three).

   scale: Logical. If TRUE (default), z-score scales the TF activity
          matrix across samples. The scaled scores of a sample then
          depend on the other samples given in the same call; use
          ‘scale = FALSE’ to get scores that can be compared between
          separate calls (e.g. a training and a test set). With fewer
          than three samples the scores are not scaled (a message is
          given).

  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves matrix in Results/ folder. Default is
          TRUE.

file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing the TF activity
          matrix to disk (‘Results/TF_matrix_<file_name>.csv’; without
          it, ‘Results/TF_matrix.csv’).

Value:

     A data frame of inferred (and, if ‘scale = TRUE’, scaled) TF
     activity scores, with samples as rows and TFs as columns. Column
     names are made syntactically valid with ‘make.names()’ (e.g.
     ‘NKX2.1’), in the returned table and in the saved file.

References:

     Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of
     computational methods to infer biological activities from omics
     data. _Bioinformatics Advances_, 2(1), vbac016.
     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

     Tuerei, D., Korcsmaros, T., & Saez-Rodriguez, J. (2016). OmniPath:
     guidelines and gateway for literature-curated signaling pathway
     resources. _Nature Methods_, 13(12), 966-967.
     https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4077

     Garcia-Alonso, L. et al. (2019). Benchmark and integration of
     resources for the estimation of human transcription factor
     activities. _Genome Research_.
     https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.240663.118

     Lachmann, A. et al. (2016). ARACNe-AP: gene network reverse
     engineering through adaptive partitioning inference of mutual
     information. _Bioinformatics_, 32(14), 2233-2235.
     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw216

     Margolin, A.A. et al. (2006). ARACNE: an algorithm for the
     reconstruction of gene regulatory networks in a mammalian cellular
     context. _BMC Bioinformatics_, 7(Suppl 1), S7.
     https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-7-S1-S7

Examples:

     ## Not run:
     
     # Downloads the CollecTRI network from OmniPath
     data("counts.norm.tuto")
     tfs_activity <- compute.TFs.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.pathway.activity
Compute pathway activity scores

Description:

     This function computes pathway activity scores from log-normalized
     gene expression data with ‘decoupleR’ (Badia-i-Mompel et al.,
     2022), based on the PROGENy resource (Schubert et al., 2018). By
     default the univariate linear model (‘"ulm"’) is used. Optionally,
     it also performs Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA) using hallmark
     signatures or any user-provided gene sets.

Usage:

     compute.pathway.activity(
       counts_norm,
       gene_sets = NULL,
       paths = NULL,
       method = "ulm",
       scale = TRUE,
       batch = NULL,
       return = TRUE,
       file_name = NULL
     )
     
Arguments:

counts_norm: A numeric matrix of log-normalized gene expression values
          (e.g. log2(TPM + 1)) with genes (symbols) as rows and samples
          as columns. A warning is given if it has values above 20,
          which log2(TPM + 1) cannot reach.

gene_sets: A named list of gene sets (character vectors of gene
          symbols; e.g., hallmark signatures or user-defined sets). If
          provided, GSVA scores will be computed for these sets.
          Default is ‘NULL’.

   paths: A data frame describing the pathway-gene interactions
          (columns ‘source’, ‘target’, ‘weight’) for use with PROGENy.
          If ‘NULL’, the human PROGENy resource (top 500 genes) is used
          and cached in ‘Results/Pathways_collection_PROGENy.csv’ (also
          when ‘return = FALSE’, so that it is downloaded only once). A
          message gives the number of pathways and interactions of the
          cached file and the date it was saved; a cached file that is
          empty or lacks the needed columns is not used (the collection
          is downloaded again, with a warning). Delete the file to
          download the collection again.

  method: Character. The ‘decoupleR’ statistic used to score the
          PROGENy pathways: ‘"ulm"’ (univariate linear model, default),
          ‘"mlm"’ (multivariate linear model), ‘"wsum"’ (weighted sum)
          or ‘"consensus"’ (consensus of the three). The gene sets of
          ‘gene_sets’ are always scored with GSVA.

   scale: Logical. If TRUE (default), each pathway is z-scored across
          the samples. The scaled scores of a sample then depend on the
          other samples given in the same call; use ‘scale = FALSE’ to
          get scores that can be compared between separate calls (e.g.
          a training and a test set). With fewer than three samples the
          scores are not scaled (a message is given).

   batch: Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the column
          order of ‘counts_norm’ (if it is named, it is matched to the
          samples by name instead). It is always treated as
          categorical. If given, the samples are split by cohort, the
          pathway activities (PROGENy and, if requested, GSVA) are
          computed and scaled (see ‘scale’) separately in each cohort,
          and the results are joined in the sample order of
          ‘counts_norm’; the output has the same form as without
          ‘batch’. Pathways or gene sets that cannot be scored in every
          cohort are left out (with a message). Default is ‘NULL’
          (single cohort); a vector with only one cohort is treated the
          same way.

  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves the score matrices in Results/
          folder. Default is TRUE.

file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing output CSV files
          (‘Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy_<file_name>.csv’ and
          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA_<file_name>.csv’; without it,
          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_PROGENy.csv’ and
          ‘Results/Pathway_matrix_GSVA.csv’).

Value:

     If ‘gene_sets’ is ‘NULL’, a data frame of PROGENy pathway activity
     scores (samples as rows, pathways as columns), scaled if ‘scale =
     TRUE’. If ‘gene_sets’ is provided, a list with two elements:

        • ‘PROGENy’: A data frame of PROGENy pathway activity scores.

        • ‘GSVA’: A data frame of GSVA scores based on the provided
          gene sets.

     Column names are made syntactically valid with ‘make.names()’
     (e.g. ‘JAK.STAT’), in the returned tables and in the saved files.
     Pathways with fewer than 5 of their genes in the data, and gene
     sets that GSVA cannot score, are left out with a message.

References:

     Schubert M, Klinger B, Kluenemann M, Sieber A, Uhlitz F, Sauer S,
     Garnett MJ, Bluethgen N, Saez-Rodriguez J. Perturbation-response
     genes reveal signaling footprints in cancer gene expression.
     Nature Communications. 2018. doi:10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
     <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6>

     Badia-i-Mompel, P. et al. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of
     computational methods to infer biological activities from omics
     data. _Bioinformatics Advances_, 2(1), vbac016.
     https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

Examples:

     ## Not run:
     
     # Compute only PROGENy activities (downloads the PROGENy model from OmniPath)
     data("counts.norm.tuto")
     pathways <- compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.WTCNA
Compute Weighted TF-coactivity Network Analysis (WTCNA)

Description:

     Construct a weighted signed or unsigned network using TF activity
     to cluster protein regulators into modules that share similar
     activity patterns. Each TF module will have a sample-level score
     represented by the eigengene of the module.

Usage:

     compute.WTCNA(
       tfs,
       batch = NULL,
       network_type = "signed",
       clustering_method = "ward.D2",
       min_module_size = 5,
       corr_mod = 0.9,
       corr_type = "spearman",
       verbose = TRUE,
       file_name = NULL,
       soft_power = NULL,
       consensus_quantile = 0,
       return = TRUE
     )
     
Arguments:

     tfs: Matrix of TF activity (samples x TFs), scaled or not: the TFs
          are standardized (within each cohort with ‘batch’) to compute
          the module eigengenes, and the other steps use correlations,
          which do not depend on the scaling. With ‘batch’, the TF
          activities of all the cohorts, each computed within its
          cohort (as ‘CellTFusion()’ does).

   batch: (Optional) A vector with the cohort of each sample, in the
          row order of ‘tfs’; if it is named, it is matched to the
          samples by name instead. It is always treated as categorical.
          If given, consensus TF modules are built across the cohorts
          (see Details) and module eigengenes are computed and scaled
          within each cohort. Default is ‘NULL’ (single cohort); a
          vector with only one cohort is treated the same way.

network_type: Network type: "signed" (default) or "unsigned".

clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering of the
          TFs (‘stats::hclust()’), applied to the TOM dissimilarity (1
          - topological overlap) between TFs, or to the consensus TOM
          dissimilarity in batch mode. Default is "ward.D2" (WGCNA's
          own default is "average": two groups of TFs are joined
          according to the average dissimilarity between their TFs).

min_module_size: Minimum number of TFs per module. Default is 5.

corr_mod: Correlation threshold (0-1): modules whose eigengenes have a
          correlation (of type ‘corr_type’) above it are merged. In
          batch mode, the correlation is computed on the eigengenes of
          all the samples, scaled within each cohort. Default is 0.9.

corr_type: Correlation used to pick the soft-threshold power, build the
          adjacency matrix, merge modules and compute the proportion of
          variance explained: "spearman" (default) or "pearson", in
          single-cohort and batch mode. The module eigengene is always
          the first principal component of the module's TF activities.

 verbose: Logical; whether to print the function messages. Default is
          TRUE.

file_name: Optional character suffix used when writing WTCNA outputs
          (CSV files and, in single-cohort mode, the diagnostic plots
          ‘Soft_Threshold_<file_name>.pdf’,
          ‘Gene_dendrogram_and_module_colors_<file_name>.pdf’ and
          ‘Gene_dendrogram_and_module_colors_after_merging_<file_name>.pdf’).

soft_power: Optional numeric value specifying the soft-thresholding
          power used to build the adjacency matrix (one value per
          cohort, in the order the cohorts first appear in ‘batch’, in
          batch mode). If ‘NULL’, the lowest power whose scale-free fit
          R^2 reaches 0.9 is chosen automatically (the power with the
          best fit if none reaches 0.9, with a message).

consensus_quantile: Numeric between 0 and 1 (batch mode only). For each
          pair of TFs, the consensus topological overlap is this
          quantile of its (calibrated) topological overlaps across the
          cohorts. With 0 (default), the minimum: two TFs are close
          only if they are close in every cohort, the strictest choice,
          which removes more TF relationships as more cohorts are
          added. Higher values are less strict: with ‘K’ cohorts,
          ‘consensus_quantile = k / (K - 1)’ takes the ‘(k + 1)’-th
          lowest value, so two TFs are close if they are close in all
          cohorts but ‘k’ (e.g. 0.25 with 5 cohorts: in at least 4 of
          them); 0.5 is the median.

  return: Logical, whether to save output plots, the module list
          (‘Results/TFs_modules_<file_name>.csv’) and the module matrix
          (‘Results/TF_module_matrix_<file_name>.csv’, with the sample
          names as row names) to "Results/" (without ‘file_name’,
          ‘TFs_modules.csv’ and ‘TF_module_matrix.csv’). Default is
          TRUE.

Details:

     TFs that WGCNA does not assign to any module (color ‘"grey"’) are
     not a module: they are left out of the module matrix and of ‘TFs
     per module’, with a message.

     In batch mode, the modules are built with the same steps as in
     single-cohort mode, on a consensus network:

       1. the samples are split by cohort, and a soft-thresholding
          power is chosen for each cohort;

       2. the adjacency and the topological overlap matrix (TOM) are
          computed in each cohort, with its own power;

       3. the TOMs are calibrated to a common scale as in
          ‘WGCNA::blockwiseConsensusModules()’: each TOM is raised to
          the power that makes its 0.95 quantile equal to that of the
          first cohort;

       4. the consensus TOM is, for each pair of TFs, the
          ‘consensus_quantile’ quantile of its calibrated TOMs across
          cohorts;

       5. the TFs are clustered on 1 - consensus TOM with
          ‘clustering_method’ and the tree is cut with the same dynamic
          tree cut as in single-cohort mode;

       6. the module eigengenes are computed and scaled within each
          cohort, and the modules are merged as in single-cohort mode
          (see ‘corr_mod’); merged scores are scaled within each cohort
          again.

     Unlike ‘WGCNA::blockwiseConsensusModules()’, the TFs of each
     module are not filtered or reassigned afterwards by their module
     membership (as in single-cohort mode). The diagnostic plots are
     only saved in single-cohort mode.

Value:

     A named list with:

        • ‘TFs module matrix’: Scaled module eigengenes (samples x
          modules), in the row order of ‘tfs’.

        • ‘TFs colors’: Vector of module colors assigned to each TF
          (‘"grey"’ for TFs not assigned to any module).

        • ‘TFs per module’: List of TF names in each module.

        • ‘Proportion of variance’: Variance explained per module
          (single-cohort mode only).

        • ‘TFs_matrix’: The TF activity matrix used (a list of
          per-cohort matrices in batch mode, in the order the cohorts
          first appear in ‘batch’).

        • ‘Network parameters’: A list with the soft-thresholding
          power(s) used (‘soft_power’, one per cohort in batch mode),
          ‘network_type’ and ‘corr_type’, used by ‘identify_hub_TFs()’,
          and in batch mode ‘consensus_quantile’.

References:

     Langfelder, P., & Horvath, S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for
     weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559.
     https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-9-559

Examples:

     data("tfs.tuto")
     network <- compute.WTCNA(tfs.tuto, corr_mod = 0.9, return = FALSE)
     
=========== identify.cell.groups
Identify cell groups

Description:

     Builds, for each TF module, a dendrogram of the deconvolution
     features significantly correlated with it. The features are
     clustered on the value of that correlation: the distance between
     two features is the absolute difference between their correlations
     with the module (e.g. 0.62 and 0.58 are at distance 0.04). Two
     features are therefore similar when they are related to the module
     to the same degree (similar biological activity), not when they
     vary together across samples. The dendrograms are cut into cell
     groups by ‘cell.groups.computation()’.

Usage:

     ## S3 method for class 'cell.groups'
     identify(
       relationship,
       clustering_method = "ward.D2",
       file_name = NULL,
       return = TRUE
     )
     
Arguments:

relationship: The list returned by ‘compute.modules.relationship()’.
          Its first two elements are used (accessed by position):

            • ‘[[1]]’ (‘correlation’): A matrix of correlations between
              TF modules (rows, named) and deconvolution features
              (columns).

            • ‘[[2]]’ (‘significant’): A list, named by TF module, of
              the features significantly correlated with each module
              (p-value, or adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’, <= the
              ‘pval’ given to ‘compute.modules.relationship()’).

          The correlations of each module are taken from the row with
          its name.

clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering
          (‘stats::hclust()’) of the features on the distance described
          above. Default: "ward.D2".

file_name: Optional character suffix for the names of the saved plots.

  return: Logical; whether to save one dendrogram plot per module to
          ‘Results/Dendrogram_cell_types_<module>_<file_name>.pdf’
          (‘Results/Dendrogram_cell_types_<module>.pdf’ without
          ‘file_name’). Each plot shows the correlation of every
          feature with the module next to its name, and its size
          follows the number of features. Default: TRUE.

Value:

     A named list of dendrograms (‘hclust’ objects, labelled with the
     feature names), one per TF module. Each one also stores the
     correlation of its features with the module (element
     ‘correlation’, used by ‘calculate_dendrogram_cuts()’). Modules
     with fewer than two significant features are discarded; ‘NULL’ is
     returned if no module remains.

Examples:

     data("network.tuto")
     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
     rel <- compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]], deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]], return = FALSE)
     dendrograms <- identify.cell.groups(rel, return = FALSE)
     names(dendrograms)
     
=========== compute.modules.relationship
Compute modules relationship

Description:

     Correlates every column of one matrix with every column of another
     (e.g., TF modules and external features such as deconvolution
     estimates or pathway activities) across the same set of samples,
     and visualizes the significant associations. It is meant for
     continuous variables only: all the columns of both matrices must
     be numeric. For categorical variables (e.g. clinical groups), use
     ‘compute.metadata.association()’.

Usage:

     compute.modules.relationship(
       matA,
       matB,
       file_name = NULL,
       batch = NULL,
       pval = 0.05,
       padj = FALSE,
       corr_type = "spearman",
       vertical = FALSE,
       return = TRUE,
       plot_grid = FALSE,
       ncol_grid = NULL
     )
     
Arguments:

    matA: A numeric matrix or data frame of continuous features
          (samples x features), e.g. TF module scores.

    matB: A numeric matrix or data frame of continuous features to
          correlate with (samples x features).

file_name: A string indicating the base name (without extension) of the
          figures to be saved in the "Results/" folder. If ‘NULL’
          (default), no figure is saved.

   batch: Optional vector indicating batch assignment for samples (no
          missing values). If it has two or more levels, partial
          correlations (‘ppcor::pcor.test()’, Pearson or Spearman
          according to ‘corr_type’) are computed controlling for batch.
          Batch is treated as categorical (one dummy variable per level
          beyond the first).

    pval: A numeric threshold for the p-value to define significance
          (p-value, or adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’, <= ‘pval’).
          Default is 0.05.

    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple
          testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, across the
          columns of ‘matB’ for each column of ‘matA’, and the adjusted
          p-values are used to define significance (in ‘significant’
          and in the figures). Default is FALSE.

corr_type: Type of correlation to compute: "spearman" (default) or
          "pearson". It also sets the type of the partial correlations
          computed with ‘batch’.

vertical: Logical; if TRUE, modules are on the x-axis and the ‘matB’
          features on the y-axis. Otherwise (default), the ‘matB’
          features are on the x-axis and modules on the y-axis.

  return: Logical; if TRUE, saves the heatmap plot as a PDF
          (‘file_name’ is needed). Default is TRUE.

plot_grid: Logical; if TRUE, generates per-pair scatter grid plots for
          significant associations, saved to
          "Results/<file_name>_scatter_grid.svg" (the 100 strongest
          pairs at most). With Spearman, the ranks of the values are
          shown, as the correlation is computed on them. With ‘batch’,
          the values shown are corrected for batch, as the correlations
          are. Default is FALSE.

ncol_grid: Integer number of columns used in scatter grid layout. If
          NULL (default), it is set to the ceiling of the square root
          of the number of panels.

Details:

     ‘matA’ and ‘matB’ must have the same samples in the same order
     (same rownames); names are compared after ‘make.names()’, so e.g.
     "TCGA-XX" and "TCGA.XX" match. Correlations and p-values use, for
     each pair of columns, the samples with a value in both (missing
     values are allowed); a pair with fewer than three such samples, or
     without variation among them, gets ‘NA’. Columns without variation
     are skipped with a message. Column names must be unique within
     each matrix.

Value:

     Invisibly, a list with:

        • ‘correlation’: the correlation matrix (columns of ‘matA’ as
          rows, columns of ‘matB’ as columns).

        • ‘significant’: a named list with, for each column of ‘matA’,
          the columns of ‘matB’ significantly correlated with it
          (p-value, or adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’, <= ‘pval’).

        • ‘p_value’: the matrix of p-values.

        • ‘p_adjusted’: the matrix of Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted
          p-values (equal to ‘p_value’ with ‘padj = FALSE’).

     If ‘return = TRUE’ and ‘file_name’ is given, a heatmap of the
     correlations is saved to "Results/<file_name>.pdf" (the ".pdf"
     extension is added if missing). Its size is computed from the
     number of features. With up to 40 features per axis, the
     significant cells show the correlation and its significance (* <
     0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001, **** < 0.0001); with more, they are
     marked with an asterisk.

Examples:

     data("network.tuto")
     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
     corr = compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]],
                                         deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]],
                                         return = FALSE,
                                         pval = 0.01)
     corr$correlation[1:3, 1:3]
     corr$significant[[1]]
     
     ## Not run:
     
     # TF modules vs PROGENy pathways (downloads the PROGENy model from OmniPath)
     data("counts.norm.tuto")
     pathways <- compute.pathway.activity(counts.norm.tuto)
     compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]],
                                  pathways,
                                  "Pathways_Progeny-TFs_Modules")
     ## End(Not run)
     
=========== compute.metadata.association
Compute associations between TF module scores and clinical metadata

Description:

     This function tests for associations between transcription factor
     (TF) module scores and available clinical traits. Numeric traits
     are correlated with each module (Pearson or Spearman) and shown as
     a heatmap. If ‘plot_grid = TRUE’, categorical traits (text, factor
     and TRUE/FALSE columns) are additionally tested with one-way ANOVA
     (Tukey HSD post-hoc) and shown as boxplot grids. All plots are
     saved in the Results/ directory, and the tables with the results
     are returned.

Usage:

     compute.metadata.association(
       scores,
       coldata,
       pval = 0.05,
       corr_type = "spearman",
       file_name = NULL,
       ncol_grid = NULL,
       plot_grid = FALSE,
       padj = FALSE
     )
     
Arguments:

  scores: A numeric matrix or data frame of TF module scores across
          samples. Typically the first element (TFs module matrix) of
          the output from ‘compute.WTCNA()’. Rows represent samples,
          columns represent TF modules.

 coldata: A data frame containing clinical traits (both categorical and
          numerical) for the same samples. Rows must be the same
          samples, in the same order, as the rows of ‘scores’ (checked
          by name; an error is raised otherwise). Numeric columns are
          treated as continuous: convert number-coded categories (e.g.
          a stage coded 1 to 4) to factor to test them as groups.

    pval: A numeric threshold (default = 0.05) to determine statistical
          significance (p-value, or adjusted p-value, ‘<= pval’). Only
          associations with (adjusted) p-values below this threshold
          are annotated in the heatmap or drawn as boxplots.

corr_type: Correlation used for the numeric traits: ‘"spearman"’
          (default) or ‘"pearson"’.

file_name: Optional character suffix of the names of the saved plots
          (‘NULL’ by default: no suffix).

ncol_grid: Integer. Number of columns in the grid of association
          boxplots. If ‘NULL’ (default), it is set to the ceiling of
          the square root of the number of panels.

plot_grid: Logical; if TRUE, tests categorical traits with ANOVA and
          saves boxplot grids. Default is FALSE.

    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple
          testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, across the
          modules for each trait, and the adjusted p-values are
          compared with ‘pval’. Default is FALSE.

Details:

     Traits that cannot be tested are skipped with a message: numeric
     traits without variation, and categorical traits with a single
     level or with as many levels as samples (e.g. a sample
     identifier). Categorical traits are only analysed when ‘plot_grid
     = TRUE’; a message lists them otherwise.

     The size of the figures is computed from their content (number of
     modules and traits for the heatmap, number of panels for the
     boxplot grids), and the y-axis of each boxplot panel from its
     data.

Value:

     Invisibly, a list with the results:

        • ‘correlation’: matrix of module-trait correlations for the
          numeric traits (modules x traits).

        • ‘p_value’: matrix of their p-values.

        • ‘p_adjusted’: matrix of their Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted
          p-values (equal to ‘p_value’ with ‘padj = FALSE’).

        • ‘anova’: data frame with the ANOVA of every module for every
          categorical trait (‘trait’, ‘module’, ‘F’, ‘p’,
          ‘p_adjusted’); ‘NULL’ if ‘plot_grid = FALSE’.

     The elements are ‘NULL’ when there is no trait of that type. The
     following files are saved to the Results/ directory:

        • ‘TF.modules_metadata_<file_name>.pdf’: a heatmap of
          module-trait correlations for numeric traits (only
          associations with p-value <= ‘pval’ are annotated, with the
          correlation and its significance: * < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** <
          0.001, **** < 0.0001).

        • ‘ANOVA_boxplot_summary_<file_name>_<trait>.svg’ (if
          ‘plot_grid = TRUE’): one boxplot grid per categorical trait
          with the significant modules.

Examples:

     data("network.tuto")
     data("traitdata.tuto")
     
     # Categorical traits (response, Enrollment.IC) are tested with plot_grid = TRUE; os and censOS are numeric
     res <- compute.metadata.association(
       scores = network.tuto[[1]],
       coldata = traitdata.tuto,
       pval = 0.05,
       file_name = 'Tutorial',
       plot_grid = TRUE
     )
     head(res$anova)

1	=========== construct_cell_groups
2	Construct cell groups based on TF networks and deconvolution
3	
4	Description:
5	
6	     A cell group is a set of deconvolution features with a similar
7	     biological activity: features related to the same TF module to the
8	     same degree (similar correlation with the module score). The
9	     features of a cell group do not need to vary together across
10	     samples. The cell groups are built in three steps:
11	
12	       1. each TF module is correlated with every deconvolution feature
13	          (‘compute.modules.relationship()’);
14	
15	       2. for each module, the significantly correlated features are
16	          clustered on their correlation with the module
17	          (‘identify.cell.groups()’);
18	
19	       3. each dendrogram is cut into cell groups, and each cell group
20	          gets one score per sample from a CCA with the score of its TF
21	          module (‘cell.groups.computation()’).
22	
23	     The deconvolution matrix and ‘network’ must have the same samples
24	     (matched by name; their order can differ): the module scores of
25	     ‘network’ are put in the sample order of the deconvolution matrix.
26	
27	Usage:
28	
29	     construct_cell_groups(
30	       network,
31	       dt,
32	       batch = NULL,
33	       pval = 0.05,
34	       padj = FALSE,
35	       corr_type = "spearman",
36	       clustering_method = "ward.D2",
37	       file_name = NULL,
38	       return = TRUE,
39	       min_cluster_size = 3
40	     )
41	     
42	Arguments:
43	
44	 network: A TF module network as returned by ‘compute.WTCNA()’ (its
45	          module scores are used).
46	
47	      dt: Deconvolution subgroups as returned by
48	          ‘multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()’; its element
49	          ‘Deconvolution matrix’ (samples x features) is used. It must
50	          have the same samples as ‘network’.
51	
52	   batch: Optional vector with the cohort of each sample: in the row
53	          order of the deconvolution matrix, or named by sample.
54	          Required when ‘network’ was built with ‘compute.WTCNA()’ with
55	          ‘batch’. With two or more cohorts, correlations and scores
56	          are corrected for cohort.
57	
58	    pval: Numeric. P-value threshold used to select the deconvolution
59	          features significantly correlated with each TF module
60	          (adjusted p-value with ‘padj = TRUE’). Default: 0.05.
61	
62	    padj: Logical. If TRUE, the p-values of each TF module are
63	          corrected for multiple testing across the deconvolution
64	          features (Benjamini-Hochberg, see
65	          ‘compute.modules.relationship()’) before selecting the
66	          significant features. Default: FALSE.
67	
68	corr_type: Correlation used between the TF modules and the
69	          deconvolution features (passed to
70	          ‘compute.modules.relationship()’): ‘"spearman"’ (default) or
71	          ‘"pearson"’. It is used to select the significant features
72	          and to cluster them.
73	
74	clustering_method: Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering of the
75	          deconvolution features of each module on their correlation
76	          with it (see ‘identify.cell.groups()’). Default: "ward.D2".
77	
78	file_name: Optional character. Suffix of the output file names (see
79	          ‘return’).
80	
81	  return: Logical. If TRUE (default), saves a PDF of the colored
82	          cell-group dendrograms
83	          (‘Results/Dendrogram_color_clusters_<file_name>.pdf’) and the
84	          composition and the scores of the cell groups
85	          (‘Results/Cell.groups.composition_<file_name>.csv’ and
86	          ‘Results/Cell.groups.scores_<file_name>.csv’).
87	
88	min_cluster_size: Integer. Minimum number of features of a cell group
89	          (minimum cluster size of the dynamic tree cut of each
90	          dendrogram). Default is 3.
91	
92	Value:
93	
94	     A named list of 3 elements:
95	
96	     Cell_groups A data frame with the projected cell group scores
97	          (samples x groups). A positive score means that the sample is
98	          on the active side of the TF module of that cell group, a
99	          negative score that it is on the inactive side.
100	
101	     Composition A named list where each element is a character vector
102	          of the deconvolution features in each group.
103	
104	     Weights A named list of CCA projection parameters (‘xcoef’,
105	          ‘train_means’, ‘train_sds’) for each group. With ‘batch’,
106	          only ‘xcoef’ is kept: test data are z-scored on their own
107	          means and SDs, as each training cohort was.
108	
109	     Cell groups are named ‘Dendrogram_<module>_group_<n>’, where ‘n’
110	     is the cluster number shown in the dendrogram PDF of that module.
111	     Features that the tree cut does not assign to any cluster are not
112	     part of any cell group (a message reports how many).
113	
114	Examples:
115	
116	     data("network.tuto")
117	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
118	     cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
119	     cell_groups$Cell_groups[1:3, 1:3]
120	     
121	=========== compute.latent_factors
122	Compute latent factors from cell group scores using NMF
123	
124	Description:
125	
126	     Decomposes the cell group scores into non-negative latent factors
127	     with Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF, ‘RcppML::nmf()’),
128	     applied to the positive part of the scores (see Details). The
129	     number of factors is chosen by bootstrap NMF if ‘rank’ is not
130	     given.
131	
132	Usage:
133	
134	     compute.latent_factors(
135	       scores,
136	       rank = NULL,
137	       ranks = 2:15,
138	       n_boot = 100,
139	       recovery_thresh = 0.7,
140	       similarity_thresh = 0.8,
141	       seed = 123,
142	       file_name = NULL,
143	       return = TRUE
144	     )
145	     
146	Arguments:
147	
148	  scores: Numeric matrix of size samples x cell groups (signed CCA
149	          composite scores).
150	
151	    rank: Integer; number of NMF factors. If NULL (default), chosen
152	          among ‘ranks’ with bootstrap NMF (see Details). If given, the
153	          stability of its factors is still computed (‘stability’).
154	
155	   ranks: Candidate ranks when ‘rank = NULL’. Default 2:15, limited to
156	          the number of cell groups (rank 1 with a single cell group).
157	
158	  n_boot: Integer; number of bootstrap NMF runs per rank. Default 100.
159	
160	recovery_thresh: Numeric; minimum recovery frequency (proportion of
161	          bootstrap runs in which the factor is found) for a factor to
162	          be robust. Default 0.7.
163	
164	similarity_thresh: Numeric; minimum cosine similarity for a bootstrap
165	          factor to count as the same factor, and minimum mean
166	          similarity for a factor to be robust. Two factors of the same
167	          rank more similar than this are considered redundant. Default
168	          0.8. Both thresholds are practical starting points, not
169	          universal cutoffs.
170	
171	    seed: Random seed used for the NMF fits and the bootstrap samples.
172	          Default 123. The caller's random number generator state is
173	          restored when the function returns.
174	
175	file_name: Optional character suffix for the saved patient-mixture
176	          plot.
177	
178	  return: Logical. If TRUE (default), saves the patient-mixture barplot
179	          to ‘Results/NMF_patient_mixture_<file_name>.pdf’
180	          (‘Results/NMF_patient_mixture.pdf’ if ‘file_name’ is ‘NULL’),
181	          and the stability plot to
182	          ‘Results/NMF_rank_stability_<file_name>.pdf’: the lowest
183	          recovery, lowest mean similarity and highest similarity
184	          between factors of each candidate rank (with the thresholds
185	          and the selected rank; only when the rank is selected), and
186	          the recovery and mean similarity of each factor of the
187	          selected rank.
188	
189	Details:
190	
191	     Only the positive part of the signed cell group scores is used:
192	     ‘max(score, 0)’, how far the sample is on the active side of the
193	     TF module of the cell group (negative scores, on the inactive
194	     side, become 0). The factors therefore describe the high-activity
195	     direction of the cell groups. The scores must not contain missing
196	     values.
197	
198	     Rank selection by bootstrap NMF (consensus of the factors across
199	     resamples of the patients). The profile of a factor is its column
200	     of ‘W’ (the weights of the cell groups). For each candidate rank:
201	
202	       1. NMF is fitted on all the samples (reference factors) and on
203	          ‘n_boot’ bootstrap samples of the patients (sampled with
204	          replacement);
205	
206	       2. the factors of each bootstrap run are matched one to one to
207	          the reference factors by the cosine similarity of their
208	          profiles (most similar pairs first), as NMF factors can come
209	          in any order;
210	
211	       3. each reference factor gets its recovery frequency and mean
212	          similarity across runs, and the factors of the rank are
213	          compared with each other to detect redundancy (two factors
214	          with almost the same profile).
215	
216	     The selected rank is the largest one whose factors are all robust
217	     and none redundant: as many factors as the data support reliably
218	     (low ranks capture the dominant patterns and are almost always
219	     stable, so the smallest stable rank would favour 2). If no rank
220	     qualifies, the rank with the most robust factors is used (the
221	     smallest in case of ties), with a message; check ‘rank_selection’
222	     and whether the main factors persist at the neighbouring ranks.
223	
224	Value:
225	
226	     A named list with:
227	
228	     Z Sample-level NMF factor scores (samples x rank). Non-negative.
229	          Each factor (column) sums to 1 over the samples: the size of
230	          each factor is in ‘nmf_model$d’ (the NMF is ‘W %*% diag(d)
231	          %*% t(Z)’). Tests on one factor at a time do not depend on
232	          this scale; to compare factors within a sample, multiply each
233	          column by its ‘d’, as done for ‘patient_mixture’.
234	
235	     W Weights of the cell groups per factor (cell groups x rank).
236	          Non-negative.
237	
238	     nmf_input The matrix fed to NMF: the positive part of the cell
239	          group scores (samples x cell groups).
240	
241	     nmf_model The ‘RcppML::nmf()’ model object (includes the scaling
242	          vector ‘d’).
243	
244	     patient_mixture Long-format data frame of per-sample factor
245	          proportions used for the mixture plot: the factor scores
246	          multiplied by the size of each factor (‘nmf_model$d’),
247	          divided by their sum in each sample.
248	
249	     stability One row per factor of the selected rank: ‘recovery’
250	          (proportion of bootstrap runs in which a matching factor is
251	          found, cosine similarity >= ‘similarity_thresh’),
252	          ‘mean_similarity’ (mean cosine similarity of the matched
253	          bootstrap factors), ‘max_similarity_other’ (highest cosine
254	          similarity with another factor of the same rank: a high value
255	          suggests redundancy) and ‘robust’ (recovery >=
256	          ‘recovery_thresh’ and mean similarity >=
257	          ‘similarity_thresh’).
258	
259	     rank_selection One row per candidate rank (‘NULL’ if ‘rank’ is
260	          given): the number of robust factors, the lowest recovery and
261	          mean similarity of its factors, the highest similarity
262	          between two of its factors, and ‘stable_distinct’ (all
263	          factors robust and none redundant).
264	
265	Examples:
266	
267	     data("network.tuto")
268	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
269	     cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
270	     latent <- compute.latent_factors(cell_groups$Cell_groups, n_boot = 20, return = FALSE)
271	     head(latent$Z)
272	     latent$nmf_model$d     # size of each factor
273	     latent$rank_selection  # stability and redundancy of each candidate rank
274	     latent$stability       # stability of the factors of the selected rank
275	     
276	=========== compute_cells_niches
277	Identify cell niches from NMF latent factors
278	
279	Description:
280	
281	     For each NMF factor, selects the cell groups that contribute most
282	     to it (the ‘top_n’ highest weights of the factor in ‘W’, see
283	     ‘extract_contributing_features()’) and describes them by their
284	     deconvolution features and CCA coefficients. Deconvolution
285	     features are kept as they are (subgroups are not expanded into
286	     their members).
287	
288	Usage:
289	
290	     compute_cells_niches(
291	       latent_factors,
292	       cell_groups,
293	       top_n = 5,
294	       return = TRUE,
295	       file_name = NULL
296	     )
297	     
298	Arguments:
299	
300	latent_factors: A list returned by ‘compute.latent_factors()’ (its ‘W’
301	          is used).
302	
303	cell_groups: The cell groups, as returned by ‘construct_cell_groups()’
304	          (its ‘Weights’ are used).
305	
306	   top_n: Integer. Number of cell groups selected per factor. Default
307	          5.
308	
309	  return: Logical. If ‘TRUE’ (default), saves the networks in
310	          ‘Results/Cells_niches_<file_name>.pdf’
311	          (‘Results/Cells_niches.pdf’ without ‘file_name’), one page
312	          per factor, and a heatmap of the NMF weights (‘W’) of all the
313	          cell groups (rows: cell groups, ordered by the factor where
314	          their weight is highest and by decreasing weight; columns:
315	          factors; outlined: the top cell groups of each factor) in
316	          ‘Results/Cells_niches_heatmap_<file_name>.pdf’.
317	
318	file_name: Character. Suffix appended to the output file name.
319	
320	Details:
321	
322	     With ‘return = TRUE’, a tree network of each factor is saved, one
323	     page per factor: the factor on the left, its top cell groups in
324	     the middle (filled with the colour of their TF module) and the
325	     deconvolution features of each cell group listed from top to
326	     bottom on the right, next to their cell group. The edge between a
327	     cell group and a feature is the CCA coefficient of the feature in
328	     the cell group score (‘xcoef’ in ‘Weights’, on the z-scored
329	     features): red if positive (the score increases with the feature),
330	     blue if negative, and wider for a larger absolute coefficient
331	     (coefficients close to zero are hairlines).
332	
333	     The factors describe the high-activity side of the TF modules of
334	     their cell groups (the NMF input is the positive part of the cell
335	     group scores). A red edge therefore means that the feature is
336	     higher in samples where the cell group is active, a blue edge that
337	     it is lower. The coefficients of features correlated with each
338	     other (e.g. several estimates of the same cell type) are estimated
339	     jointly, so a single coefficient can be small or have the opposite
340	     sign of the others of its cell group even when the feature itself
341	     is related to the TF module like them: read the sign of a single
342	     edge together with the rest of its cell group.
343	
344	Value:
345	
346	     A data frame with one row per factor, selected cell group and
347	     feature: ‘factor’, ‘cell_group’, ‘module’ (TF module of the cell
348	     group), ‘weight’ (NMF weight of the cell group in the factor),
349	     ‘feature’ and ‘coefficient’ (CCA coefficient of the feature in the
350	     cell group score). Rows are ordered by factor and by decreasing
351	     weight.
352	
353	Examples:
354	
355	     data("network.tuto")
356	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
357	     cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto, return = FALSE)
358	     latent <- compute.latent_factors(cell_groups$Cell_groups, return = FALSE)
359	     niches <- compute_cells_niches(latent, cell_groups, return = FALSE)
360	     head(niches)

362	=========== scores.stat.analysis
363	Perform statistical analysis on scores using a specified test
364	
365	Description:
366	
367	     Unified interface for testing associations between any score
368	     matrix and a clinical/experimental trait. Accepts cell group
369	     scores, NMF latent factors (output of ‘compute.latent_factors()’),
370	     or any samples x features matrix.
371	
372	Usage:
373	
374	     scores.stat.analysis(
375	       scores,
376	       coldata,
377	       trait,
378	       test = c("fisher", "wilcox", "anova", "kruskal", "ttest"),
379	       pval = 0.05,
380	       padj = FALSE
381	     )
382	     
383	Arguments:
384	
385	  scores: A list, NMF output from ‘compute.latent_factors()’, or a
386	          score matrix (samples x features). When a list, the first
387	          element must be the score matrix; optional second and third
388	          elements (e.g. the output of ‘construct_cell_groups()’) are
389	          subsetted to the significant features and returned with their
390	          names.
391	
392	 coldata: A data frame (or tibble) containing clinical or experimental
393	          metadata for samples. Must include the column specified in
394	          ‘trait’. Its rows are matched to the samples of the scores by
395	          row name; without sample names, they must be in the order of
396	          the scores. Samples with a missing trait are left out.
397	
398	   trait: Character. The name of the column in ‘coldata’ representing
399	          the clinical or experimental trait to test against (e.g.,
400	          response, subtype, etc.). It must be categorical.
401	
402	    test: Character. Statistical test to perform. One of:
403	
404	            • ‘"fisher"’ - Fisher's exact test (scores binarised at
405	              median)
406	
407	            • ‘"wilcox"’ - Wilcoxon rank-sum test (non-parametric,
408	              binary traits)
409	
410	            • ‘"anova"’ - One-way ANOVA (parametric, two or more
411	              groups)
412	
413	            • ‘"kruskal"’ - Kruskal-Wallis test (non-parametric, two or
414	              more groups)
415	
416	            • ‘"ttest"’ - Welch's t-test (parametric, binary traits)
417	
418	          Only one can be used per call; defaults to the first one
419	          (‘"fisher"’).
420	
421	    pval: Numeric. Threshold for significance: a feature is significant
422	          if its (adjusted) p-value is ‘<= pval’ (default: 0.05).
423	
424	    padj: Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple
425	          testing across the features with the Benjamini-Hochberg
426	          method, and the adjusted p-values are compared with the
427	          threshold. Default FALSE.
428	
429	Details:
430	
431	     The function automatically calls the corresponding statistical
432	     test function based on the ‘test’ argument:
433	
434	        • ‘scores.fisher.test()’
435	
436	        • ‘scores.wilcox.test()’
437	
438	        • ‘scores.anova.test()’
439	
440	        • ‘scores.kruskal.test()’
441	
442	        • ‘scores.ttest()’
443	
444	     Each test produces both a statistical result and visual outputs
445	     (PDF plots) stored in the ‘"Results/"’ folder for the significant
446	     features. These visualizations include the relevant test results
447	     (p-values) annotated on the plots.
448	
449	Value:
450	
451	     A list whose first element is the score matrix restricted to the
452	     significant features (no column if none is significant). Optional
453	     second and third elements (from the input list, e.g. the
454	     composition and weights of the cell groups) are subsetted
455	     accordingly and keep their names. The last element, ‘Statistics’,
456	     is a data frame with the test of every feature (‘feature’, ‘test’,
457	     ‘statistic_name’, ‘statistic’, ‘p_value’, ‘p_adjusted’,
458	     ‘significant’).
459	
460	Examples:
461	
462	     data("network.tuto")
463	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
464	     data("traitdata.tuto")
465	     cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
466	     sig <- scores.stat.analysis(cell_groups, traitdata.tuto, trait = "Enrollment.IC",
467	                                 test = "kruskal", pval = 0.05, padj = TRUE)
468	     head(sig$Statistics)
469	     names(sig$Composition)
470	     
471	=========== compute_composite_score
472	Compute composite score for cell groups
473	
474	Description:
475	
476	     Computes a composite score by performing Canonical Correlation
477	     Analysis (CCA) between the deconvolution features of a cell group
478	     and the score of its TF module (module eigengene). The score is
479	     the weighted sum of the (scaled) features of the cell group, with
480	     the weights of the first canonical component: the combination of
481	     the features that correlates most with the TF module score (with a
482	     single module score, this is the linear regression of the module
483	     score on the features, up to a scaling factor). As the sign of CCA
484	     weights is arbitrary, the score is oriented so that it is aligned
485	     with the TF module: a positive score means that the sample is on
486	     the active side of the module for that cell group. The score
487	     therefore increases with the features of the cell group when they
488	     are positively related to the module, and decreases with them when
489	     they are negatively related.
490	
491	Usage:
492	
493	     compute_composite_score(cell_group, module, network, batch = NULL)
494	     
495	Arguments:
496	
497	cell_group: A numeric matrix of cell deconvolution features for a cell
498	          group (samples x features), with sample names as row names.
499	          The module score of ‘network’ is matched to these samples by
500	          name; every sample must be in the network.
501	
502	  module: Character. Name (color) of the TF module the cell group was
503	          built from; must match a column name of the module matrix in
504	          ‘network’ exactly.
505	
506	 network: Output of compute.WTCNA() (single- or multi-cohort).
507	
508	   batch: Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the row
509	          order of ‘cell_group’. It is treated as categorical: the cell
510	          group features are z-scored within each cohort (mean 0, SD 1
511	          per cohort; a feature constant in a cohort is 0 there) before
512	          the CCA. The module score is used as it is: ‘compute.WTCNA()’
513	          already scales it within each cohort.
514	
515	Details:
516	
517	     The CCA is reliable only when the number of features of the cell
518	     group is well below the number of samples. When it reaches the
519	     number of samples, the first canonical correlation is 1 whatever
520	     the data, the weights are not unique and the score is decided by
521	     numerical noise. Cell groups with many features and few samples
522	     (e.g. cross-validation folds) are the most affected.
523	
524	Value:
525	
526	     An unnamed list of two elements:
527	
528	        • ‘[[1]]’: Numeric matrix (samples x 1) with the composite
529	          score, i.e. the scaled cell group features projected onto the
530	          first canonical component, oriented to be aligned with the TF
531	          module. With ‘batch’, it has mean 0 within each cohort.
532	
533	        • ‘[[2]]’: Projection parameters used to score new samples:
534	          ‘xcoef’ (canonical weights of the first component),
535	          ‘train_means’ and ‘train_sds’ (column means/SDs used for
536	          scaling). The sign of ‘xcoef’ follows the orientation of the
537	          score. When batch correction was applied, only ‘xcoef’ is
538	          returned: new samples are then z-scored on their own means
539	          and SDs, as each training cohort was.
540	
541	Examples:
542	
543	     data("network.tuto")
544	     data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
545	     cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
546	     group <- names(cell_groups$Composition)[1]
547	     module <- sub("^Dendrogram_(.*)_group_.*$", "\\1", group) # TF module of the cell group
548	     features <- deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]][, cell_groups$Composition[[group]], drop = FALSE]
549	     score <- compute_composite_score(features, module, network.tuto)
550	     head(score[[1]])
551	     
552	=========== compute.modules.enrichment
553	Compute TF module enrichment using directed target genes
554	
555	Description:
556	
557	     This function performs enrichment analysis for transcription
558	     factor (TF) modules using known TF-target interactions. For each
559	     module, it takes the hub TFs and retrieves their known targets
560	     from the TF-target network (CollecTRI by default). It then
561	     conducts an over-representation analysis (ORA) against the
562	     Reactome pathway database. To reduce redundancy, only unique
563	     pathways per module are retained by filtering out overlaps between
564	     modules.
565	
566	Usage:
567	
568	     compute.modules.enrichment(
569	       counts_norm,
570	       hub_tfs,
571	       TF.collection = "CollecTRI",
572	       universe = NULL,
573	       cancer_type = NULL,
574	       top_n = 10,
575	       file_name = NULL
576	     )
577	     
578	Arguments:
579	
580	counts_norm: A numeric matrix of normalized gene expression values.
581	          Rows are gene symbols, columns are samples. This matrix is
582	          used to restrict the universe of genes used in enrichment and
583	          validate TF-target gene presence.
584	
585	 hub_tfs: A list of hub TFs per module, typically obtained using
586	          ‘identify_hub_TFs()’. This should be a list of two elements:
587	          one with named hub TFs per module, and another with their
588	          module membership or additional metadata. Only the modules in
589	          this list (those with hub TFs) are analysed.
590	
591	TF.collection: Character. The TF-target network from which the targets
592	          of the hub TFs are taken: ‘"CollecTRI"’ (default),
593	          ‘"Dorothea"’ (confidence A and B) or ‘"ARACNE"’, read as in
594	          ‘compute.TFs.activity()’. Use the collection the TF activity
595	          was computed with.
596	
597	universe: Optional. A user-specified data frame of TF-target
598	          interactions (columns ‘source’ and ‘target’), used instead of
599	          ‘TF.collection’.
600	
601	cancer_type: Optional character. Cancer type used to locate the ARACNe
602	          network (input/ARACNE/<cancer_type>/network/network.txt),
603	          only used when ‘TF.collection = "ARACNE"’. If ‘NULL’, the
604	          network is auto-detected when only one exists under
605	          input/ARACNE/.
606	
607	   top_n: Integer. Number of pathways shown in the dot plot of each
608	          module. Default is 10. All the pathways are in the returned
609	          tables.
610	
611	file_name: Optional character suffix for the names of the saved plots.
612	
613	Details:
614	
615	     The targets of the hub TFs are taken from the TF-target network
616	     (for CollecTRI and Dorothea, cached in
617	     Results/TF_target_collection_<TF.collection>.csv), and
618	     ‘ReactomePA::enrichPathway()’ is used for ORA with the Reactome
619	     database. The ORA input is the 20% most variable targets of the
620	     module's hub TFs; a module with fewer than 5 such genes is skipped
621	     with a message. The background is all the genes of ‘counts_norm’.
622	     Any set of TFs has targets enriched in the pathways those TFs
623	     regulate, so the results describe what the hub TFs of each module
624	     regulate, not evidence that the module itself is special. Pathways
625	     enriched in more than one module are removed, so only
626	     module-specific results are kept. TF names are matched in their
627	     syntactic form too (e.g. ‘NKX2.1’, as returned by
628	     ‘compute.TFs.activity()’, matches ‘NKX2-1’).
629	
630	Value:
631	
632	     Invisibly, a list with two elements, each a named list with one
633	     table per module (the result table of
634	     ‘ReactomePA::enrichPathway()’, or ‘NULL’ for a module without
635	     enrichment):
636	
637	        • ‘enrichment’: the module-specific pathways (adjusted p-value
638	          < 0.05, and not significant in any other module).
639	
640	        • ‘enrichment_all’: all the significant pathways of each
641	          module, before removing those shared between modules.
642	
643	     For each module with module-specific pathways, a dot plot is also
644	     saved in the Results/ directory as a PDF file named
645	     Enrichment_Reactome_Module_<color>_<file_name>.pdf
646	     (Enrichment_Reactome_Module_<color>.pdf without ‘file_name’). If
647	     no enrichment is found for a module, a message is given and no
648	     file is saved for that module. An error is raised if none of the
649	     hub TFs is in the TF-target network, or if none of their targets
650	     is found in the row names of ‘counts_norm’ (they must be gene
651	     symbols).
652	
653	Examples:
654	
655	     ## Not run:
656	     
657	     # Identify the hub TFs of a TF network from compute.WTCNA()
658	     hub_tfs <- identify_hub_TFs(wgcna_network, mm_thresh = 0.8, degree_thresh = 0.9)
659	     
660	     # Perform module-level Reactome enrichment
661	     enr <- compute.modules.enrichment(counts.norm, hub_tfs)
662	     head(enr$enrichment[[1]])
663	     ## End(Not run)
664	     
665	=========== identify_hub_TFs
666	Identify hub TFs
667	
668	Description:
669	
670	     Identifies hub TFs per module using values of module membership
671	     and degree. TFs with high module membership (correlation of their
672	     activity with the module score > ‘mm_thresh’, with the correlation
673	     used to build the network, ‘corr_type’ of ‘compute.WTCNA()’) and a
674	     degree at or above the ‘degree_thresh’ quantile of their module
675	     are considered hub TFs. The degree of a TF is its intramodular
676	     connectivity, as in WGCNA: the sum of its network adjacencies with
677	     the other TFs of the same module. The adjacencies are computed as
678	     in ‘compute.WTCNA()’, with the same soft-thresholding power,
679	     network type and correlation (for a ‘"signed"’ network, ((1 +
680	     r)/2)^{power}, so a negative correlation adds almost nothing
681	     instead of being subtracted).
682	
683	Usage:
684	
685	     identify_hub_TFs(network, mm_thresh = 0.8, degree_thresh = 0.9)
686	     
687	Arguments:
688	
689	 network: TF network obtained from ‘compute.WTCNA()’.
690	
691	mm_thresh: Threshold for module membership. Default is 0.8.
692	
693	degree_thresh: Quantile threshold for degree within each module.
694	          Default is 0.9 (top 10%).
695	
696	Details:
697	
698	     The TF activities are taken from ‘network’ (element ‘TFs_matrix’)
699	     and matched to the module scores by sample name. For a
700	     multi-cohort network (‘compute.WTCNA()’ with ‘batch’), the
701	     per-cohort TF activities are stacked to compute the membership,
702	     and the degree is the mean of the per-cohort degrees (each with
703	     the power of its cohort).
704	
705	     Networks built before the soft-thresholding power was stored in
706	     ‘network’ (element ‘Network parameters’) have their power chosen
707	     again with the rule of ‘compute.WTCNA()’ (with a message),
708	     assuming a signed network and Pearson correlation.
709	
710	Value:
711	
712	     A list with two elements:
713	
714	     hubGenes Named list of hub TFs per module. Modules without hub TFs
715	          are left out (a message lists them).
716	
717	     detailedData Data frame with one row per hub TF (TF names as row
718	          names) and the columns ‘Module’, ‘ModuleMembership’ and
719	          ‘Degree’.
720	
721	Examples:
722	
723	     data("network.tuto")
724	     
725	     hub_tfs <- identify_hub_TFs(network.tuto, mm_thresh = 0.8, degree_thresh = 0.9)
726
